textes.Au fond du coffre, gravé dans le bois :: At the bottom of the chest, engraved in the wood: “To the one who gave the Great Moai his eyes back, and the Hall of Song its voice. Thank you. — The Elders (and the little Moai, who helped carry).”
textes.Au fond du cul-de-sac, un coffre tout co: At the end of the dead end, a very sticky chest. Inside: a vial of sap, some coins… and a label: “Property of the slimes. Do not touch.” Too late.
textes.Au nord de ton village, il y a un cercle: North of your village, there's a circle of standing stones. On my Ancients' map, there's a serpent drawn right in the middle. The ground sounds hollow there, {surnom}. A shovel would work wonders.
textes.Au pied du phare, sous une pierre qui lu: At the foot of the lighthouse, under a glowing stone: an iron box full of coins, and a note: “For the next one who sees it. — T.”
textes.Au sommet des murailles de Dité, trois s: At the top of the walls of Dité, three figures spread their wings: the FURIES! “Nobody enters Dité!” they cry, diving at you.
textes.Au sommet du Grand Temple, offrir une ja: At the top of the Great Temple, offer a jar of rain to Tlaloc (blue shrine) and copal to Huitzilopochtli (red shrine)
textes.Au sommet du Mont Fusain: At the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Au sommet du Temple de Kukulkan, mettre: At the top of the Temple of Kukulkan, set the two calendar wheels to the date of the creation of the world (the great stele on the square shows it; Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it)
textes.Au sommet du massif, il y a un endroit d: At the top of the massif, there's a spot where you can see both your islands at once. I mapped it. On a shell, naturally.
textes.Au village, il y a Sylwen et son pain de: In the village there's Sylwen and her honey bread, Aëlwen and her potions, Faelar and his stories… Go and see them, they're all waiting for you.
textes.Au-delà, il n'y a plus que la mer et les: Beyond this there's only the sea and the clouds: turn back!
textes.Au-dessus de la porte, en lettres de feu: Above the door, in letters of fire: “YOU WHO ENTER HERE, KEEP HOPE (AND TAKE A COAT).” Lower down, smaller: “The ferryman only accepts obols. No coins with holes.”
textes.Aucun ne brille encore. Il faudra sans d: None are shining yet. You'll probably need to wake the crystal in each wing.
textes.Aucun pour l'instant. Rendez service, et: None yet. Help people out, and they will remember it.
textes.Aucune pour l'instant. La première t'att: None yet. The first one may be waiting for you under the village…
textes.Aucune quête en cours. Parlez aux habita: No quest in progress. Talk to the locals: many of them need help.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai deux îles. Celle de l': Today, I have two islands. The Mother Tree's, where Sylwen always keeps a honey loaf for me and Nimiel lies in wait with a hundred questions. And this one, where an old man waves his hat at the mist, and a blacksmith grumbles at the trees while stroking them. My mother says my heart is split in two. I think it has simply grown.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève avant Clou, ce q: These days, I get up before Clou, which isn't hard: he sleeps on the cash box. I beat iron until noon, I sell in the afternoon, I count in the evening. Clou means “nail”: I named him after my first one. Bent, but he holds. Customers climb up, complain about the prices, buy anyway. That's enough for me. Almost.
textes.Aurélien Lumen m'apprendra le sort de lu: Aurélien Lumen will teach me the light spell if I bring him three moon shards that fell on the island. Then I'll have to awaken the runes in the Crypt.
textes.Aux commandes du Glisseur stellaire: At the controls of the Star Glider
textes.Aux pieds d'Ehécatl : la tablette du Sol: At the feet of Ehécatl: the tablet of the Sun of the Wind… and a large pink conch, the god's conch. When you blow into it, the wind rises.
textes.Avalé par une grenouille (et recraché): Swallowed by a frog (and spat out)
textes.Avant le naufrage, Octave a ressemelé me: Before the shipwreck, Octave resoled my boots with the leather of his own belt. He held his trousers up with a rope until the end of the voyage. I never thanked him. The left one is at the bottom of the sea, but the right one is still going strong.
textes.Avant mon départ, elle m'a donné un sach: Before I left, she gave me a little bag of herbs: “Half for the Tree, the other half for you, on the evenings when you cry.” I gave it all to the Tree. She knows. She's been pretending to be cross ever since.
textes.Avant, elle s'appelait Églantine. C'étai: She used to be called Églantine. She was our queen… The brambles took her heart.
textes.Avant, j'étais cartographe du roi. J'ai: I used to be the king's cartographer. I drew a map of this kingdom so precise it was as big as the kingdom itself. Nobody ever unfolded it.
textes.Avec beaucoup de clous. Et de la bonne v: With lots of nails. And goodwill. Mostly nails.
textes.Avec joie ! Que l'Aube nous garde… et qu: With joy! May the Dawn watch over us… and over my feet too, I trip a lot. Let's go!
textes.Avec la pelle, cherche les petites croix: With the shovel, look for the little wooden crosses on the sand. Castaways hid their savings there. It glints a bit, up close.
textes.Avec moi ? Non : à ta place. Un guerrier: With me? No: in my place. A jaguar warrior against jaguars, Cuauhtli finds that far too funny, he won't let me go. The slopes of Smoking Mountain, to the west, under the pines. When a jaguar crouches, it's about to pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Avec ta pelle sur l'épaule, tu as l'air: With that shovel on your shoulder, you look like a real treasure hunter. Found anything?
textes.Avec une pelle ? Il faut une hache pour: With a shovel? You need an axe to fell this tree.
textes.Avec une pelle, on trouve de tout dans l: With a shovel, you'll find all sorts in the beach sand: shells, castaways' coins… I sell shovels, you know. Just saying.
textes.Avec ça, tu vas faire des jaloux. Surtou: With that, you'll make people jealous. Especially the neighbour. The neighbour gets jealous of everything.
textes.Aventurier de rang S, légende de la Guil: Rank S adventurer, legend of the Guild
textes.AÏE ! Dans MA cabane ?! Les prix doublen: OUCH! In MY hut?! Prices are doubling!
textes.AÏE ! La lave ! Tu bondis hors du cratèr: OUCH! The lava! You leap out of the crater, clutching your backside.
textes.Aëlwen m'a soignée cent fois depuis ma n: Aëlwen has healed me a hundred times since I was born. Her potions are bitter and her hands are gentle: you have to take both together.
textes.Aïe ! La lave brûle ! (Les démons, eux,: Ouch! The lava burns! (The demons soak their feet in it… you don't.)
textes.Aïe ! Pas dans la sauce : elle est brûla: Ouch! Not in the sauce: it's scalding! (And besides, it stains.)
textes.Aïe ! Qui a mis ce caillou ici ?: Ouch! Who put this pebble here?
textes.Aïe aïe aïe ! La lave du Phlégéthon ! Tu: Ow ow ow! The lava of the Phlegethon! You leap back onto the bank, your soles smoking. Take a raft next time.
textes.BAC DES PIÈCES DÉTACHÉES\nNe pas tomber:
SPARE PARTS BIN
Do not fall in.
(The sorting robot would file you under “Miscellaneous”.)
textes.BIIIP. Le lecteur clignote en rouge : «: BEEEEP. The reader flashes red: “BADGE NOT DETECTED. Have you tried having a badge?” (Up there, on the back mezzanine, something is shining…)
textes.BIP BIP ! Un chariot élévateur robot te: BEEP BEEP! A robot forklift bumps into you: “FORKLIFTS HAVE PRIORITY. THANK YOU FOR YOUR UNDERSTANDING.” Look carefully before crossing the aisles.
textes.BIP. Surface propre à 97 %. Les 3 % rest: BEEP. Surface 97% clean. The remaining 3% is your shoes.
textes.BLORP ! (Il fait défiler les hologrammes: BLORP! (He flips through the holograms: a mayor sucking in his tummy, a tavern-keeper glaring, a baron with three hats, a crested granny raising her fist.) They're PERFECT! They're so… so Heavyfoot! I'm sending everything to Mama! (Click-click-click. A long silence. Then the device goes “beep”.) She replied! She says: “My Glorb, you have friends!” … (He wobbles very hard.) I have friends. Here, my kaleidoscope glasses: with them, you see the world like I do. In a thousand pieces, and all of them pretty.
textes.BLOUOP ! Le Roi Gélatineux retombe de to: BLOOP! The Jelly King slams back down with all his weight: the ground shakes!
textes.BONK ! L'Alouette heurte l'obstacle et s: BONK! The Alouette hits the obstacle and folds up all at once… The harness spring set you down gently. Nothing broken!
textes.BOOONG ! (Les adeptes disent qu'il ne fa: BOOONG! (The followers say you must never strike it three times in a row. Nobody remembers why.)
textes.BOOONG ! Le grand couvercle de cuivre ré: BOOONG! The great copper lid rings out across the whole forecourt. Above the temple, the Great Flying Spaghetti wriggles all its noodles.
textes.BOOONG. Quelque part dans les gradins, q: BOOONG. Somewhere in the stands, someone shouts: “AGAIN!” (The champion is allowed.)
textes.BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG ! Le sol tremble: BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG! The ground trembles a little. Up above, Mount Bolognese starts to rumble… It sounds like it heard you.
textes.BOUM ! Le rocher t'aplatit comme une crê: BOOM! The boulder flattens you like a pancake (a very offended pancake). You peel yourself off the floor at the entrance of the corridor. Next time: an alcove!
textes.BOUM ! … Voilà, tout est par terre. Même: BOOM! … There, everything's on the floor. Even me, almost. Thanks, here, a cookie from our place. It floats too, careful.
textes.BOUM. BOUM. BOUM. Tes coups résonnent da: BOOM. BOOM. BOOM. Your knocks echo through the mountain… A deep voice behind you: “No use knocking, big one. Nobody enters Forgefer without being invited.” It's Bramm, the guard. Talk to him.
textes.BOUUUUH ! … Hé. Tu n'as même pas eu peur: BOOOO! … Hey. You weren't even scared?
textes.BRAMM : « OUVREZ LA GRANDE PORTE ! » Un: BRAMM: “OPEN THE GREAT GATE!” A rumble, creaking chains… and the two iron doors slowly open onto the glow of the Forgefer forges.
textes.BRRRANG ! Une guitare saturée, une basse: BRRRANG! A fuzzed-out guitar, a rumbling bass: two musicians rehearse in the middle of the yurt, between the stove and an old amp.
textes.BZZT. Une lampe rouge clignote : « MONTE: BZZT. A red lamp flashes: “FREIGHT LIFT RESERVED FOR MANAGEMENT. Please defeat management first.”
textes.Ba Sidi dit que vous avez un tapis ancie: Ba Sidi says you have an old carpet that shows the way to the seal.
textes.Ba-da-boum, ba-da-boum ! Tu as trouvé le: Ba-da-boom, ba-da-boom! You found the rhythm of the Flower Camp.
textes.Bah… il n'y avait plus grand-chose dedan: Meh… there wasn't much left in it anyway.
textes.Barnabé ! Dix-sept traversées, pas un ro: Barnabé! Seventeen crossings, not one rock. A legend, oh yes!
textes.Barnabé ! Tu as encore salué la brume, h: Barnabé! You waved at the mist again last night.
textes.Barnabé ? Le meilleur cartographe du roy: Barnabé? The best cartographer in the kingdom, according to him. The worst, according to the rock. We used to be friends. Used to is a long way back.
textes.Barnabé dessinait les cartes. Sa carte d: Barnabé drew the maps. His map said “open sea”. The sea said “rock”. I believed the map. Twenty-two years I've regretted it.
textes.Barnabé dit que sa carte des Anciens mon: Barnabé says his map of the Ancients shows “a golden eye in the east”. That's the Mother Tree. He has good eyes, for a human.
textes.Barnabé parle à la mer comme à une vieil: Barnabé talks to the sea like an old friend. Humans say he's mad; the trees say he's kind. I believe the trees.
textes.Barnabé t'a parlé de moi ? Laisse-moi de: Barnabé told you about me? Let me guess: “it was Octave at the helm”. He's a broken record, that one.
textes.Basile Pinceau, le peintre du village, a: Basile Pinceau, the village painter, saw the pot of blue (no. 1) floating on the Rubbed-Out Pond the day after the Great Downpour. It got stuck on a giant water lily, far from the bank. Basile swims like a stone.
textes.Basile est à l'Étang Gommé, Lili sur la: Basile is at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Lili on the White Strand.
textes.Basile, j'ai repêché le pot de bleu !: Basile, I fished out the pot of blue!
textes.Basile, qu'est-ce que vous regardez dans: Basile, what are you looking at in the pond?
textes.Bastien ? Un pêcheur qui se lève tôt et: Bastien? A fisherman who gets up early and doesn't haggle too much. We get along: he fishes, I pay. Not much.
textes.Bastien. Combien, la sardine, aujourd'hu: Bastien. How much for a sardine today?
textes.Battre son record à Dragon-Pixel: Beat your high score at Dragon-Pixel
textes.Bedaine vous troque ce caillou-qui-chant: Bedaine swaps you this singing pebble.
textes.Bedaine, le tanuki du Marché aux trocs,: Bedaine, the tanuki of the Barter Market, wants to teach you the Great Swap: a pebble that, swap after swap, becomes a treasure.
textes.Belle matinée, oui. Il faut en profiter: Lovely morning, yes. Best enjoy it before the heat.
textes.Belles ? Elles sont AFFICHE-NANTES ! … B: Nice? They're POSTER-PERFECT! ... Well. Pigment painted the rat, I printed the letters, and we argued about the colour for three hours. She wanted green, I wanted black. We went with green. The next Great Boucan has to be the biggest of all time, with people coming from everywhere! But our posters can't swim. You travel. You could carry three: one to Paulo, the cook of Port-Azur; one to Ulric, the innkeeper of Montjoie; and one to Tom the Fiddler, the musician at the Crâne Fendu, on Balafre. Great encounters start with a poster!
textes.Bernard défie quiconque de courir de la: Bernard challenges anyone to run from the fountain to the lighthouse in under a minute.
textes.Beurk ! La grenouille t'a avalé…\n(Il fa:
Yuck! The frog swallowed you…
(It's pitch black, it smells of mud, and it's very, very sticky.)
textes.Bien caché, un petit sac de pièces ! Le: Well hidden, a little bag of coins! The captain's treasure! (He's asleep. He'll never know his parrot talked.)
Nice and hot, just as it should be.
textes.Bien sûr ! Du cacao, du piment, un peu d: Of course! Cacao, chili, a little vanilla, and water. Sugar? What's sugar?
textes.Bien sûr ! On déterre, on déterre… Voilà: Of course! We dig, we dig… There! Grilled fish, coconut, and… oh no, that's a hot stone. Don't eat it. Well, if you want, but it crunches.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens. Les elfes n: Of course I remember. Elves forget nothing: sometimes that's a problem.
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre veux-tu parler ?: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre voulez-vous parler: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. J'ai dormi dans les branches, et u: Well. I slept in the branches, and a bird woke me up singing out of tune. It was charming.
textes.Bien. Te voilà apprenti d'Arcanelle. Éco: Good. So you're an apprentice of Arcanelle. Listen: six masters, six spells. Aurélien Lumen will teach you light, Pyra fire, Borée frost, Zéphyrine levitation, Théophraste telekinesis, and Mère Sauge healing. Each will ask you for something: magic isn't given, it's traded. When your spellbook has its six spells, come back to me.
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. J'ai vendu une pe: Good. Very good, even. I sold a shovel this morning. To you, maybe?
textes.Bien. Très bien. (Pyrus frappe le sol de: Good. Very good. (Pyrus strikes the ground with his pitchfork.) In the name of the Guard: thank you. Here, something to warm you up.
textes.Bien. Un bricoleur, c'est un futur clien: Good. A tinkerer is a future customer. A good tool changes everything, you'll see.
textes.Bien. … (Hector frappe, chauffe, frappe: Good. … (Hector hammers, heats, hammers again.) … There. A bronze cog, as precise as a captain's watch. Take it to Hortense.
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, les poissons nage: Welcome! At our place, the fish swim all through the house: it's more cheerful. Want to feed them?
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, on ne laisse pas: Welcome! Here, we never let a visitor leave without a glass of tea. The first glass is gentle as life…
textes.Bienvenue ! Je prépare le cacao. Le secr: Welcome! I'm preparing the cacao. The secret is the foam: you pour from one pot to the other, from very high. Want to try?
textes.Bienvenue au Cabaret des Cailloux ! Tien: Welcome to the Pebble Cabaret! Here, listen to this one:
textes.Bienvenue au Café Feedback. Chocolat cha: Welcome to Café Feedback. Hot chocolate, three coins. Herbal tea, two coins. Melancholy is free. The jukebox only plays one song, but it's the right one.
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Concours de Grimaces: Welcome to the Great Grimace Contest! Watch closely, here we go: one, two, three… GRIMACE! … (All three pull… exactly the same face. The same one as always.) So? Who won?
textes.Bienvenue au chantier, capitaine ! Ici,: Welcome to the shipyard, captain! Here we plane, nail, and tar… and dream of the open sea.
textes.Bienvenue au musée ! Enfin… chez moi. Ma: Welcome to the museum! Well… my home. But it's a museum. Have you seen my collection?
textes.Bienvenue chez le Disquaire ! Ici, il y: Welcome to the Record Shop! Here you'll find every record on the island. Vinyle lets me mind the shop when he goes out for some fresh air. Take your time.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est petit, mais c: Welcome to my home! It's small, but it's warm and smells good.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est tout rond, c': Welcome to my home! It's all round, it's all warm, and it smells lovely.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! Va dire bonjour à t: Welcome to my home! Go say hello to everyone. Even Grommelot. Especially Grommelot: he loves being ignored.
textes.Bienvenue chez un chevalier de Montjoie: Welcome to the home of a knight of Montjoie! I'm polishing my armor for the tournament. Want to help?
textes.Bienvenue dans la Guilde ! Le tableau de: Welcome to the Guild! The quest board is right behind you: four new contracts every day. Bring them back to me, I stamp them, and you go up in rank. And now that you're registered, the adventurers in the tavern might want to team up with you. Talk to Sister Pétronille, Violette and Sir Tancrède. All three of them have… a little problem.
textes.Bienvenue dans ma collection ! Deux mill: Welcome to my collection! Two thousand records. Pick one, I'll put it on the turntable.
textes.Bienvenue dans mon atelier ! Attention a: Welcome to my workshop! Watch out for the wires. And the sparks. And the cat. Want to help me test my machine?
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île Al Dente !\nAu nord:
Welcome to Al Dente Island!
To the north: Mount Bolognese (it spits sauce).
To the west: the Colander Temple.
Please do not eat the signs.
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île de Larsen !\nÀ l'oue:
Welcome to Larsen Island!
West: the Flower Camp.
East: Rainville (take an umbrella).
In the middle: the Main Stage.
textes.Bienvenue… Respire. Il reste un tapis, l: Welcome… Breathe. There's one mat left, the yellow one, by the door. Sit down, close your eyes, and listen to the wind on the canvas. Want to try?
textes.Bip ! Je fais comme Zéro. Bip !: Beep! I'm doing like Zéro. Beep!
textes.Bip, bip… clonk ! Synthé-Soda goût fruit: Beep, beep… clonk! Moon-fruit flavor Synth-Soda. Nobody knows what Moon fruits taste like.
textes.Bip-bip ! Le lecteur passe au vert : « B: Beep-beep! The reader turns green: “WELCOME, ROBOT NO. … ERROR … WELCOME ANYWAY.” The door sinks into the floor. Below, something very big breathes like an engine.
Beep. This furniture no longer belongs to you. Beep.
textes.Biscotte ! (Le petit rat saute de ton ép: Biscotte! (The little rat hops from your shoulder to his, nibbles his ear, then goes back to yours.) See? He chose you. He always goes back to your shoulder. (Petit-Pierre sniffles.) It's okay. He'll be better off with you, travelling, than here with Mange-Clous and his ladle. He's very clever, you know: when he disappears down a hole, he always comes back with something. A coin, a button, a pearl… Rats know where the treasures are. Here, my cabin boy's coins. And if you don't have a whistle yet to call your animals, take this one: Gwen carved it for me from a bone, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig carved around it. Whistle, and Biscotte will come back. And you'll come see me again, right? With him?
textes.Biscotte arrive en trottinant et te tire: Biscotte trots over and tugs your shoelace: “Shall we go?”
textes.Biscotte grimpe le long de ton bras et s: Biscotte climbs up your arm and settles on your shoulder, tail around your neck. He's at home.
textes.Biscotte saute de ton épaule et file ver: Biscotte hops off your shoulder and scurries home, zigzagging.
textes.Biscotte se dresse sur ton épaule, renif: Biscotte rears up on your shoulder, sniffing the salty air: “Ah, the smell of the hold!”
textes.Biscotte, un petit rat blanc et brun, vi: Biscotte, a little white and brown rat, lives in the hold of the Requin Borgne. He's the secret friend of Petit-Pierre, the cabin boy. But Mange-Clous, the cook, has sworn to throw him overboard: his cheeses keep disappearing. Petit-Pierre would like Biscotte to go off with someone kind before it's too late. To lure him out of the hold, you need aged cheese.
textes.Bizarre ? Hé ! Je t'interdis. … Bon. Un: Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
textes.Bizarre, oui. C'est le mot. Je n'aurais: Weird, yes. That's the word. I couldn't have put it better.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Tu ne {le} connais pas: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Vous ne {le} connaissez: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre… oui, peut-être. Mais qui ne l'e: Weird… yes, maybe. But who isn't, around here?
textes.Blorp ! Pour maman ! Elle est restée sur: Blorp! For Mama! She stayed on Gloop, she's too squishy to travel, so I send her photos of everything. But I'm missing the most important part: the people down below! The real Heavyfeet, on their islands! I don't dare go down. I'm green, I wobble, and the last time I said hello to a fisherman, he yelled “A GIANT JELLY!” and jumped into the water. Could you do it? Take my holo-camera. Photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, the lady from the pirate tavern, the Baron of Montjoie and the crested granny of Boucan. Four corners of the archipelago! Mama will bounce for joy!
textes.Bof. Gaston boude, la mer est grise dans: Meh. Gaston is sulking, the sea is grey inside my head, and I've lost my favourite spoon.
textes.Bon vent, {surnom} ! Et méfie-toi des li: Fair winds, {surnom}! And watch out for the vines on the right.
textes.Bon vent. Et si tu vois Barnabé… ne lui: Fair winds. And if you see Barnabé… don't tell him anything.
textes.Bon, d'accord : qu'est-ce qui est gris,: All right, fine: what's grey, very tall, and doesn't move? … Me when I'm asleep. And me when I'm awake. Hee hee!
textes.Bon, par où on va maintenant ?: So, which way do we go now?
textes.Bon, pour {objet}, ça fera {prix}. Clou,: Right, for {objet}, that'll be {prix}. Clou, put that away. No, don't eat it.
textes.Bon. BON ! Prends-le. Gratuitement. Tu m: Fine. FINE! Take it. For free. You wore me down. But don't tell anyone: I have a reputation as a businesswoman. Well, businessman. Anyway.
textes.Bonjour ! Excuse le désordre. Enfin, l'o: Hello! Excuse the mess. Well, the order. Well… everything's on the ceiling, you know.
textes.Bonjour ! Je suis Grigri, le virus le mo: Hello! I'm Grigri, the cheapest virus in the world!
textes.Bonjour ! Tu as un bout de fromage ? Mêm: Hello! Do you have a bit of cheese? Even a small one?
textes.Bonjour ! Tu tombes bien, c'est l'heure: Hello! You've come at just the right time, it's breakfast. Are you hungry?
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Gaston et moi discutio: Hello, hello! Gaston and I were just talking about you. Well, mostly Gaston.
textes.Bonjour, Doyenne. Halo m'envoie vous sal: Hello, Elder. Halo sent me to greet you.
Good morning, Octave. Your kapok tree says hello.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit ! Attention où tu met: Hello, dear! Watch where you step: there's a cat everywhere.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit. Je tricote des pulls: Hello, dear. I knit plaid sweaters for the whole street. When it rains, you need to be warm. And when it doesn't rain… it rains anyway, here. Want a pair of socks? I have too many.
textes.Bonjour. … Bonjour ! Bonjour, bonjour, b: Hello. … Hello! Hello, hello, hello! Sorry. It's been so long. (His voice is a little deep, a little crackly, like an old radio.) Thank you, my friend. Mio will be so happy. And Cargo… he kept it for me, didn't he? He keeps everything, that big softie. Here: these are the two sodas I had in my treasure hatch. For twenty years. They still sparkle.
textes.Bonsoir. Mon voisin humain trouve que je: Good evening. My human neighbor finds me good company.
textes.Bon… si tu changes d'avis, tu sais où me: Well… if you change your mind, you know where to find me.
textes.Borin Barbe-de-Fer ? Un nain qui croit q: Borin Barbe-de-Fer? A dwarf who thinks good iron grows under his mountain. Good iron is made by the arm. He forges well. I'll never tell him so.
textes.Borin grave trois runes sur ta lame et l: Borin engraves three runes on your blade and feeds them at the heart of the magma. They light up, blue, and never go out again. “A king's blade, lad.”
textes.Borin rive des écailles de bronze sur ta: Borin rivets bronze scales onto your mail, like the skin of a dragon. “Dwarves wore these in the days of the Great Mines.”
textes.Borée Givrelin m'apprendra le gel si je: Borée Givrelin will teach me frost if I bring him three everlasting frost flakes from the northern cliffs. Then I'll have to cross the Mirror Lake to the Frost Crystal.
textes.Bouleversée ? Je suis… je suis… (Elle tr: Upset? I'm… I'm… (She trips over nothing.) Sorry. My sun rosary! Father Clotaire gave it to me for my fifteenth birthday. I was praying by the lake for Monsieur Yvon, and an enormous, ENORMOUS frog stuck out its tongue and… slurp. It swallowed it. Monsieur Yvon calls it the Duchess. Frogs spit out what they swallow when you beat them, apparently. Would you please… ? I'll pray. From afar. From very far.
textes.Boum, ba-da boum ! Le djembé résonne aut: Boom, ba-da boom! The djembe echoes around the fire… and, somewhere in the camp, another drum answers you.
textes.Bravo ! Tu as tenu… presque une minute !: Bravo! You lasted… almost a minute! Next time, we'll tackle sit-ups.
textes.Brindille a perdu ses gouttes de rosée p: Brindille lost her dewdrops everywhere. There are even some at the very top of the cave!
textes.Brindille, la factrice ailée, s'est foul: Brindille, the winged postwoman, has sprained a wing. There are three letters left to deliver: to Grumbald, the innkeeper, to Ombreline, the librarian, and to Gorgoth, the arena champion.
textes.Brioche ? La chatte rousse ? (Elle souri: Brioche? The ginger cat? (She smiles.) Oh yes. She comes onto the terrace when I knit. She pretends to sleep, and as soon as the ball of yarn rolls… hop! She catches it, nibbles it, and gives it back. Well, almost. As it happens: this morning, a red ball of yarn fell out of my basket. It rolled into the hotel garden. I didn't have time to look for it: Monsieur Edmond was calling me about the laundry. Take it, if you find it. For Brioche, it's a treasure.
textes.Brioche arrive… quand elle a décidé d'ar: Brioche arrives… when she has decided to arrive. Tail held high.
textes.Brioche bondit sur un papillon… et le ra: Brioche pounces on a butterfly… and misses. She grooms herself as if nothing happened. It was on purpose.
textes.Brioche monte dans la barque du bout des: Brioche steps into the boat on tiptoe. Water everywhere! She sits at the front, deeply offended.
textes.Brioche rentre à la maison sans se retou: Brioche goes home without looking back. She'll be back. If she feels like it.
textes.Brioche se frotte contre tes jambes, ron: Brioche rubs against your legs, purrs loudly, then pretends not to know you. That's her way of saying yes.
textes.Briser le sceau des Abysses: Break the seal of the Abyss
textes.Brrr ! L'eau noire est glaciale… Tu rega: Brrr! The black water is freezing… You swim back to the south shore.
textes.Brrr ! Le froid du Cocyte te mord les do: Brr! The cold of the Cocytus bites your fingers. A coat, in the Vestibule… the inscription did say so.
textes.Brrr. Une maison vide, des toiles d'arai: Brrr. An empty house, cobwebs in every corner… and a chest, over there, at the back.
textes.Brrrt-brrrt… La photocopieuse crache une: Brrrt-brrrt… The photocopier spits out a sheet: “FORM REJECTED. Stamping order not compliant. Please start again from the beginning. Thank you for your administrative patience.” The red “SEEN” marks fade by themselves. (Reread the staff memo, near the entrance.)
textes.Bruit de Fond ! C'est ce que dit la vois: Background Noise! That's what the neighbor says. We took it as a compliment.
textes.Brutus, le forgeron de Port-Coutelas, me: Brutus, the blacksmith of Port-Coutelas, will forge me an iron fist if I bring him three crocodile teeth from the Drowned Marsh.
textes.Bucatini, il me faut de la sauce de la M: Bucatini, I need some sauce from the Cooking Pot for the sacred Dish.
textes.Bzzt. Elle t'envoie. Évidemment. (Il sou: Bzzt. She sent you. Of course. (He sighs and shows his tablet: a zigzagging curve.) Right. The Heart lost three shards last night. One fell near the Observatory, one in the Species Greenhouse, among the gurgles, and the third… somewhere up high, in the Zero-Gravity Garden: up there, it'll never fall back by itself. Bring them to me. With three astral crystals, I can weld them back together. Then they'll have to be put back in the Heart. At the very top. A hundred and ten metres. It's nothing. Well, it's something.
textes.Bzzzt ! Nouvelles couleurs pour les carp: Bzzzt! New colors for the carp.
textes.Bzzz… Je vais bien. Mes cheveux, un peu: Bzzz… I'm fine. My hair, a little less.
textes.Bzzz… Veuillez soulever les pieds. Merci: Bzzz… Please lift your feet. Thank you. BEEP.
textes.Bénédiction de l'Aube ! Frappe, maintena: Blessing of the Dawn! Strike now, strike!
textes.C'EST LE GRAND BOUCAN ! La Halle est ple: IT'S THE GREAT BOUCAN! The Hall is packed to the rafters: Paulo and his cooking pot, Ulric and his frogs, Tom the Fiddler on a barrel… Rouille points at the pit: “You! In the pit! NOW!”
MINE! Oh no, it's a pebble.
textes.C'est Sardine ! Mon chien ! Il est parti: It's Sardine! My dog! He ran off this morning after a Lisse robot. He's always chasing robots, he thinks they're giant boxes of kibble! He has a red bandana, one ear up, one ear down, and he smells a bit like fish. I've looked all over town. Chaussette says her dogs picked up his scent toward the Scrapyard. But Mum won't let me go to the Scrapyard alone. Would you go? Please? His name is Sardine. He comes when you whistle. Well, when he feels like it.
textes.C'est ce que disait ta carte. Juste avan: That's what your map said. Right before the rock.
textes.C'est ce que tu disais à quarante ans, a: That's what you said at forty, with your ankle on backwards.
textes.C'est comment, la vie au camp ?: What's life like at the camp?
textes.C'est de la poésie ! La poésie, ça grand: It's poetry! Poetry makes people bigger.
textes.C'est elle ! C'est elle ! Hugo ! HUGO !: It's her! It's her! Hugo! HUGO! … Thank you. You've given us back our honeymoon. What you're feeling right now, deep in your heart? That's happiness. Keep it.
textes.C'est fini ! Je l'ai poussé dans la corb: It's over! I pushed it into the trash, and emptied the trash. Come see me, I have a few words to say to Mister Fil…
textes.C'est gentil ! On le lui dira. Tiens, pr: How kind! We'll tell him. Here, have a slice of cake, we made far too much.
textes.C'est justement ÇA qui est drôle ! HA HA: That's exactly what's FUNNY! HA HA HA!
textes.C'est l'heure de manger. Mon ventre me l: It's time to eat. My tummy keeps reminding me.
This is when everyone gets busy. I like that sound.
textes.C'est moi qui ai cueilli la menthe !: I'm the one who picked the mint!
textes.C'est moi qui paie les glaces. (Elle cro: I'm paying for the ice creams. (She crosses her arms, pouts… then bursts out laughing.) You beat me! Nobody has ever beaten me! Except a seagull, once, but the seagull cheated, it caught the wind. You know what? It's the best race of my life. Here: two cosmic jellies, which are rarer than ice cream, and a few washers for the ice cream anyway. And a rematch tomorrow! And the day after! For life!
textes.C'est parti ! Garde-les à l'œil… tous le: Here we go! Keep an eye on them… all four.
textes.C'est pour l'humain ! Tu lui donneras ?: It's for the human! Will you give it to them? Please!
textes.C'est pour ça qu'elle marche. Tiens-toi: That's why it works. Stand up straight, and drink your tea.
textes.C'est quoi, votre programme exceptionnel: So what's this exceptional programme of yours?
textes.C'est toi ! Mon ami l'humain sans cornes: It's you! My hornless human friend! Look, I learned to make a flame! … Okay, it's a small flame. A spark. But it's mine!
textes.C'est toi. En carré. Ocre a mis du jaune: It's you. All square. Ocre has put yellow around your head: “You shine, because you smooth.” The little stick figures around it raise their arms. They look very impressed.
textes.C'est un escargot sur le dos d'une tortu: It's a snail on a turtle's back. What does it shout?
textes.C'est un manche. Avec un tout petit peu: That's a handle. With a tiny bit of iron on the end.
textes.C'est vrai ? Tu veux bien ? Il s'appelle: Really? You'll do it? His name is Miou. He's ginger, with a twisted ear, like this. (She twists her ear.) Khety says cats like to go to the dead, on the plateau, near the square tombs. But Mama doesn't want me to go there all alone. Will you bring him back? Promise?
textes.C'est vrai ?! Personne ne m'avait jamais: Really?! Nobody ever told me that! Here, keep a page of my score. It'll be worth a fortune when I'm famous.
textes.C'est ça, file. Les coquillages, eux, ne: That's it, run off. Seashells, at least, never leave.
textes.C'est ça. Attention à la troisième march: Right. Mind the third rung of the ladder, it creaks.
textes.C'est-à-dire que… si je te le vends, je: The thing is… if I sell it to you, I won't have it anymore. See the problem?
textes.C'est… c'est vrai ? Tu ne manges pas les: Is… is that true? You don't eat little demons? … Phew! Here, it's my favorite brioche. You can have it. But just one!
textes.C'est… gentil. Je vais le poser là, à cô: That's… nice. I'll put it there, next to the other thing I don't know how to use.
textes.C'était… une feinte. Une feinte très ava: That was… a feint. A very advanced feint.
textes.CAMAZOTZ, LA CHAUVE-SOURIS DE LA MORT !: CAMAZOTZ, THE BAT OF DEATH! He cut off Hunahpu's head, says the Popol Vuh. Dodge his dives, strike when he lands.
textes.CERBÈRE ! Trois têtes, trois gueules de: CERBÈRE! Three heads, three mouths of fire. They say he can't resist honey cakes… one per head.
textes.CIPACTLI, LE MONSTRE DE LA TERRE ! Les d: CIPACTLI, THE EARTH MONSTER! The gods made the world from its body. It dives and resurfaces: keep moving, strike when it lunges.
textes.CLONK ! « RANGEMENT AUTOMATIQUE EN COURS: CLONK! “AUTOMATIC TIDYING IN PROGRESS.” Claws descend from the ceiling and put every crate back in its place, very politely.
textes.CRAAAC ! Le rocher se fracasse contre le: CRAAACK! The boulder smashes against the stone threshold, into a thousand pebbles. (A thousand steps, a thousand pebbles: it's home.)
textes.CRAC ! Le mur s'ouvre. De l'autre côté :: CRACK! The wall opens. On the other side: a kitchen, a pie… and a dwarf woman with her rolling pin raised.
textes.Caelan joue encore la même chanson…: Caelan is playing the same song again…
textes.Caillou-papier-ciseaux. Ils jouent toujo: Rock-paper-scissors. They always play rock. They win one time out of three.
textes.Camazotz hurle : une nuée de chauves-sou: Camazotz screeches: a swarm of bats rises!
textes.Camazotz pousse un cri à vous percer les: Camazotz lets out a cry that pierces your eardrums!
textes.Camazotz s'écrase sur les dalles et se d: Camazotz crashes onto the flagstones and dissolves into a cloud of bats fleeing through the cracks in the vault. Silence… On the altar at the back, something green lights up.
textes.Camp des Fleurs\nPaix, amour et tourneso:
Flower Camp
Peace, love and sunflowers.
(Please don't walk in the gardens.)
textes.Capitaine, le Révérend a besoin de la Râ: Captain, the Reverend needs the Golden Grater.
textes.Capucine Buvard, la fleuriste, a vu un l: Capucine Buvard, the florist, saw a rabbit roll the pot of red (no. 3) towards Mr Paille, the scarecrow, in the middle of the White Meadows. But the grass is tall, and Capucine is scared of rabbits.
textes.Capucine est aux Prés Blancs, Achille au: Capucine is in the White Meadows, Achille at the foot of the Ink Waterfall.
textes.Capucine, pourquoi ces fleurs sont-elles: Capucine, why are these flowers all white?
textes.Capucine, voici le rouge ! Le lapin s'es: Capucine, here's the red! The rabbit ran away.
textes.Cargo, Kenji cherche une puce vocale Sér: Cargo, Kenji is looking for a Z Series voice chip, for Zéro.
textes.Carène : le bateau en bouteille: Carène: the ship in a bottle
This bench is our meeting room.
textes.Ce champignon qui brille, c'est quoi ?: That glowing mushroom, what is it?
textes.Ce coffre a des dents ! UNE MIMIQUE ! Qu: This chest has teeth! A MIMIC! When the lid opens wide, it's about to pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Ce formulaire est déjà tamponné. (Deux f: This form is already stamped. (Twice would be overzealous. Zeal is forbidden on Tuesdays.)
This little wall is mine. So is the town.
textes.Ce n'est pas encore le moment pour celui: It's not time for that one yet.
textes.Ce poing de fer, tu me le forges ?: That iron fist… will you forge it for me?
This post is my morning newspaper.
textes.Ce qui me ferait plaisir ? %s. Je ne dis: What would make me happy? %s. I never say no to that.
textes.Ce qui me ferait plaisir ? Une visite, c: What would make me happy? A visit, like this one. That's already a lot.
textes.Ce robot sent le boulon. Je peux le mord: This robot smells of bolts. Can I bite it? Say yes.
That red one is for Flanelle.
textes.Ce soir à la Grande Scène : « Le Soleil: Tonight on the Main Stage: “The Sun and the Rain”! Flanelle sings, Grésil makes his guitar squeal, and Arc-en-Ciel answers Bourrasque's drums.
textes.Ce soir à la batterie : Gédéon Lisse ! L: Tonight on drums: Gédéon Lisse! His opening drumroll makes the glass roof shake. Rouille howls with joy.
textes.Ce soir, on danse sous l'Arbre-Mère ?: Tonight, shall we dance beneath the Mother Tree?
textes.Ce sont des attrape-rêves. Le filet attr: These are dreamcatchers. The net catches bad dreams, and good dreams slide through the little hole in the middle, down the feathers, to the sleeper. Want one? It's made with twine from Galet.
textes.Ce trou ? C'est Truffe, mon gars. Le plu: That hole? That's Truffe, my lad. The smallest of my pigs. Pink and black, as big as a bread basket, and a nose… a golden nose! He smells truffles underground from fifty paces. But there it is: he smells turnips too. And my turnips, when you dig them up, they wake up and run away! The other day, he woke up twelve. Twelve! Germaine ran all the way to the mill. So Truffe runs off every morning toward the woods, and with my knees, I can't catch him anymore. He had a little bell so we could hear him coming. He lost it. A pig like him needs someone who walks a lot, who travels, who likes surprises under the ground. Someone like you, actually. Go see Germaine: she always knows where he's wandering.
textes.Ceci est un avis d'expulsion. Bonne jour: This is an eviction notice. Have a nice day!
That one, I call Little Sauce.
textes.Celui-là ? Il est bien trop beau pour êt: That one? It's far too beautiful to be sold. That's why it's in the window.
textes.Celui-là est arrivé ce matin. C'est le p: That one arrived this morning. It's the oldest in the shop!
textes.Cerbère ? Ha ! Ce gros toutou ! Trois tê: Cerberus? Ha! That big pup! Three heads, three cakes, and he sleeps like a baby. I'm happy to bake them, but I haven't a drop of fire honey left. The fire bees nest in two old hollow trunks in the Ash Wood. Bring me two honeycombs. Gently: they sting, but they're polite.
textes.Cerbère crache le feu de ses trois gueul: Cerbère breathes fire from all three mouths!
textes.Cerbère s'effondre, ses trois têtes ense: Cerbère collapses, all three heads together. (“He'd have preferred cakes,” whispers a little voice in your head.) The south gate opens.
textes.Ces crocodiles… je peux t'aider ?: Those crocodiles… can I help you?
textes.Ces pierres levées, au nord du village…: Those standing stones, north of the village… It wasn't the elves who raised them. Someone older still.
textes.Cet arbre porte une entaille : il s'abat: This tree bears a notch: it can be felled… with an axe.
This item will come in handy later.
textes.Cette botte… c'est celle de Barnabé ! Je: This boot… it's Barnabé's! I'd know it anywhere, I resoled it myself. I'll buy it for {prix} coins. He'll never see it again. HA!
textes.Cette canne… c'est moi qui l'ai taillée,: That rod… I carved it myself, twenty-two years ago, on the deck of the Stubborn Seagull. Barnabé gave it to you? The thief.
textes.Cette fenêtre va disparaître dans 3… 2…: This window will disappear in 3… 2… (no, it's staying).
textes.Cette fois, je vais te faire peur pour d: This time, I'm going to scare you for real!
textes.Cette île ? Une jungle, {surnom}. De la: This island? A jungle, {surnom}. A real one. Those big pale trees over there are kapok trees. They're older than my socks.
textes.Ceux-là, ce sont les fées qui les font p: Those ones, the fairies grow them. One bite, and hop, you wake up above the clouds.
textes.Chambre sept… non, elle est prise. Chamb: Room seven… no, it's taken. Room nine, sea view. Good night.
textes.Champs de Blé Dur\nIci pousse le blé des:
Durum Wheat Fields
This is where pasta wheat grows.
No pasta without wheat, no wheat without sun.
textes.Chaque nuit, Rê traverse le monde d'en d: Every night, Ra crosses the underworld in his boat, and Apophis, the serpent of chaos, wants to swallow him. Since the Pyramid of Ra was sealed, Néferet no longer hears Ra singing at dawn.
textes.Chaque pouvoir lancé rend de l'endurance: Every power you cast gives back stamina; every four powers, half a heart.
textes.Chaque printemps, les navets de Père Gau: Every spring, Père Gaubert's turnips wake up and run off across the Southern Fields. With his bad knees, he can't catch a single one any more. He'd like five golden turnips, caught during a Great Turnip Alert.
textes.Chaque semaine, Bastien me monte son pan: Every week, Bastien brings his basket of fish up to me. We argue over the price of every sardine. He says “Peuchère”, I say “Cash”, and we always end up at last week's price. That's our way of saying hello.
textes.Chaque soir, il agite son chapeau vers l: Every evening, he waves his hat at the mist. Where I come from, nobody answers. One evening, I did: three flashes of a lantern, from the highest platform. He danced on his beach until midnight. He doesn't know it was me.
textes.Charge plus longtemps (la lueur devient: Charge longer (the glow turns blue): when you release, you spin and strike all around you, twice. In VR: click the right stick.
textes.Charger remplace la partie en cours : pe: Loading replaces the current game: remember to save first.
textes.Charon grogne : « Déjà payé. Monte. » Et: Charon grunts: “Already paid. Get in.” And the boat glides over the black water.
textes.Charon, le passeur, te regarde de ses ye: Charon, the ferryman, looks at you with his golden eyes: “An obol to cross. No obol, no boat. And don't tell me you forgot it, they all say that.” (There was a bowl of obols in the Vestibule…)
textes.Chasser cinq slimes dans les prés: Hunt five slimes in the meadows
textes.Chasser deux grenouilles géantes au lac: Hunt two giant frogs at the lake
textes.Chasser deux mimiques (les vrais coffres: Hunt two mimics (the real chests thank you)
textes.Chasser dix gobelins (la Guilde a besoin: Hunt ten goblins (the Guild needs socks)
textes.Chasser huit grenouilles géantes (le lac: Hunt eight giant frogs (the lake is overflowing with croaks)
textes.Chasser la Duchesse, la Grenouille Reine: Hunt the Duchess, the Frog Queen of the lake (she ate a rowing boat)
textes.Chasser le virus de ton carnet : casser: Chase the virus out of your journal: break its three locks on the screen (if you take a break, Glitch helps you pick up again: near the Arcade Station in the morning and evening, in the arcade in the afternoon)
textes.Chasser les chiens d'enfer sauvages du c: Drive the wild hellhounds out of the lava field (east of the Great Blaze)
textes.Chasser les gargouilles des Ruines de l': Drive the gargoyles out of the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium (on the north-western cliffs of the island)
textes.Chasser les grenouilles géantes du Lac d: Hunt the giant frogs of the Frog Lake (east of Montjoie, through the East Gate; watch out for their tongues, they swallow you up)

Hunt the giant frogs of the Frog Lake (east of town, through the East Gate): the biggest one, the Duchess, will give back the sun rosary; then bring it back to Sister Pétronille (at the Temple of Dawn, in the Upper Town, or at the Guild in the afternoon)
textes.Chasser quatre gobelins au Bois des Luti: Hunt four goblins in the Goblin Wood (they steal socks)
textes.Chasser quatre squelettes dans le donjon: Hunt four skeletons in the dungeon (they frighten the mimics)
textes.Chasser trois loups au Bois des Lutins (: Hunt three wolves in the Goblin Wood (at night)
textes.Chasser trois slimes bleus (ils tachent: Hunt three blue slimes (they stain the washhouse laundry)
textes.Chercher Miou sur le plateau de Rê, près: Look for Miou on the plateau of Ra, near the mastabas (the square tombs), and pick him up in your arms (E)
textes.Chercher Pépin dans le Bois de Cendre (a: Look for Pépin in the Ash Wood (south-east of the city, under the ember trees) and call him (E)
textes.Chez nous, on dirait : « que tes racines: Where I come from, we'd say: “may your roots run deep”.
textes.Choisis un talent pour le lire. Les tale: Pick a talent to read it. The talents of a branch are learned in order, from top to bottom.
textes.Chut ! Je fais entrer un trois-mâts dans: Shh! I'm getting a three-master into a bottle. All that's left is to pull the thread to raise the masts. Want to do it?
textes.Chut ! Je suis à deux doigts d'une décou: Shh! I'm on the verge of a discovery. Or an explosion. Do you want to press the button?
textes.Chut ! On joue à cache-cache ! Trois pet: Shh! We're playing hide-and-seek! Three little Moai have hidden under the rocks. Find them! … And don't lift the real rocks too hard, they're touchy.
textes.Chut ! Parle moins fort ! (Il regarde pa: Shh! Not so loud! (He looks all around.) It's about Biscotte. He's a rat. My rat. Well, the ship's rat, but he's my friend. He's tiny, white with brown spots, and he sleeps in my hammock when the captain isn't looking. Only, Mange-Clous lost three cheeses, and he swore on his ladle that he'd throw “that filthy rat” overboard! Biscotte isn't filthy! He washes three times a day! I'm just a cabin boy, I can't have a rat of my own, the captain says a cabin boy owns nothing. But you… could you take him? He likes shoulders and cheese. Mostly cheese. Go see Mange-Clous: if he knows Biscotte is leaving, he might give you something to lure him. He's grumpy, but he's not bad at heart. Just a bad cheese.
textes.Chut ! Tu es devant Nefer-Miou, la chatt: Shh! You are before Nefer-Miou, the sacred cat of the house. She descends from great Bastet herself. We owe her respect!
textes.Chut. Je prie. Enfin, je pense aux pâtes: Shh. I'm praying. Well, I'm thinking about pasta. Same thing.
textes.Chut… Quelqu'un dort. Et il ronfle comme: Shh… Someone's sleeping. And snoring like a forge bellows.
textes.Chut… Trois enfants dorment sur des futo: Shh… Three children sleep on futons of every color. All you hear is the wind on the canvas, and a mother knitting.
textes.Chut… ah, c'est toi. Tu tombes bien : j': Shh… ah, it's you. Just in time: I need an opinion. Want to listen?
textes.Chut… ça mord peut-être. Non. Bon. Je pê: Shh… maybe something's biting. No. Oh well. I'm fishing.
textes.Chuuut. Quelqu'un chantonne tout bas : «: Shhh. Someone is humming very softly: “Sleep, little hammer…”
textes.Cinq ! Cinq beaux dorés ! (Il les caress: Five! Five beautiful golden ones! (He strokes them one by one, like little kittens.) You caught them gently, I can see. Not a single bump. They just look a bit offended. They'll get over it. They always do.
textes.Cinq blagues des petits Moaïs: Five jokes from the little Moai
textes.Cinq cents mètres de corde de chanvre, e: Five hundred metres of hemp rope, tightly coiled. Each end is closed with a funny knot: the friendship knot, says Galet. The harder you pull, the tighter it holds.
textes.Cinq coquillages nacrés ! Ma collection: Five pearly shells! My collection is complete! Here, take my old compass, and a few coins. You've earned them, {surnom}!
textes.Cinq pièces, mon chou. Même les hamacs,: Five coins, dear. Even hammocks cost money here. Especially the hammocks: they've seen things.
textes.Cinq… et tous intacts. Regarde comme ils: Five… and all intact. Look how they shine, even in broad daylight. Tonight, the bridges of Ramure will be blue like they used to be. You have a gentle heart, little one, and gentle hands too. Here: fox ears, sewn by Pivoine. Put them on, and all of Ramure will know you're one of us.
textes.Cipactli balaie tout de sa queue !: Cipactli sweeps everything away with its tail!
textes.Cipactli plonge… et resurgit ailleurs !: Cipactli dives… and resurfaces somewhere else!
textes.Cipactli s'effondre dans un grondement d: Cipactli collapses with a mountain's rumble. His body turns to stone, earth, roots… as on the first day, when the gods made the world from his body. On the altar at the back, a green feather begins to glow.
textes.Citoyen d'honneur, ça se mérite ! Rendez: Honorary citizen, that has to be earned! Do favours for our residents: ten favours, and I'll hand you the key to the town in front of everyone, with a fanfare. Well, with Django.
textes.Clac ! Le bras du tourniquet tombe, la l: Clack! The turnstile arm drops, the lamp turns green, and the iron shutter sinks into the floor. “STAFF EXIT AUTHORISED. HAVE A GOOD DESCENT.” The service stairs lead to the Assembly Line.
textes.Clac ! Un grondement, et les deux poids: Clack! A rumble, and the two weights slide back to their starting places.
textes.Clac ! Une lampe s'allume au-dessus de l: Clack! A lamp lights up above the door… and above your head, something very heavy goes “crrrr”. RUN! (The alcoves are free.)
textes.Clac-clac-FLOP ! L'Alouette se déplie au: Clack-clack-FLOP! The Alouette unfolds above you in mid-fall… and the canvas billows out. You're gliding!
textes.Classe conseillée : aventurier. (La boul: Recommended class: adventurer. (The ball recommends that to everyone.)
textes.Clic : choisir • double-clic : utilise: Click: select  •  double-click: use  •  I / Tab / Esc: close
textes.Clic, clac, cliquetis ! L'hélice tourne,: Click, clack, cliquetis! The propeller turns, the chain sings. Pedal, and up she goes! A little. It's not a rocket, it's an Alouette.
textes.Clic, clic, clic… Une grand-mère tricote: Click, click, click… A grandmother knits in a red armchair, surrounded by balls of yarn. Plaid sweaters dry on a line.
textes.Clic. La bibliothèque pivote… un passage: Click. The bookcase swivels… a secret passage!
textes.Clic… FIOU ! Une fléchette jaillit du mu: Click… WHIZZ! A dart shoots out of the east wall! The dark, cracked tiles are trapped: step on the light ones.
textes.Clique sur les tuiles pour les tourner :: Click the tiles to rotate them: connect the battery ⚡ to the antivirus ✚.
textes.Cliquetis, la cité des ingénieurs fous —: Cliquetis, the city of mad engineers — the Inventions Fair, the Zephyr, the cable car
textes.Cliquetis, la ville des inventeurs, en d: Cliquetis, the city of inventors, is overflowing with them
textes.Clonk ! Les trois lampes du synoptique p: Clonk! The three lamps on the diagram turn green: ALL BELTS GO TOWARD THE EXIT. (The intern would be proud. Well, if he understood.)
textes.Clonk ! Une canette de Synthé-Soda tombe: Clonk! A can of Synth-Soda drops into the tray. It's ice cold, and it glows a little in the dark.
textes.Clou (en fouillant ta poche) : « Hiii hi: Clou (rummaging in your pocket): “Heeee hee hee!”
textes.Clou ? Il est arrivé un matin, il a volé: Clou? He showed up one morning, stole my last coin, and stayed. We get along fine: we both love money.
textes.Clou a du rythme. Amène-le à la teuf, pe: Clou's got rhythm. Bring him to the party, peuchère!
textes.Clou fait tinter une pièce qu'il vient d: Clou jingles a coin he just took from you… and Octave takes it back.
textes.Clou fouille, trouve une miette, la mang: Clou rummages, finds a crumb, eats it, and falls asleep on your shoulder. He's adopted you. So have I, a little.
textes.Clou s'est caché derrière le comptoir. O: Clou is hiding behind the counter. You can only see his tail.
Clou tugs at your sleeve and holds out his hand.
textes.Clou veut savoir s'il peut fouiller tes: Clou wants to know if he can go through your pockets. He's asking, that's new.
textes.Clou, cache la caisse, voilà du monde !: Clou, hide the cash box, we've got company!
textes.Clou, tu as vu ? Il frappe le marchand !: Clou, did you see that? Hitting the shopkeeper! I'll remember this.
textes.Clémence veut peindre avec des couleurs: Clémence wants to paint with natural colours: a red coral from the bottom of the bay, some honey and a coconut.
textes.Colline du Feedback\nQuand le vent souff:
Feedback Hill
When the wind blows hard, the hill whistles,
like a guitar too close to its amp.
textes.Combien de cercles compte ce royaume ?: How many circles does this realm have?
textes.Comme chaque matin depuis mille ans. Et: Like every morning for a thousand years. And I never tire of it.
textes.Comme disait ma grand-mère : jamais de c: As my grandmother used to say: never wear socks on the sand.
textes.Comme le roc, Octave ! Ton fer chante so: Solid as a rock, Octave! Your iron sings under the bass.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un Moaï qui danse ?: What do you call a dancing Moai?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un chien qui n'a pa: What do you call a dog with no legs?
textes.Comment attirer le perroquet de la capit: How do I lure the captain's parrot?
textes.Comment devenir citoyen de Port-Azur ?: How do I become a citizen of Port-Azur?
textes.Comment rejoindre ton île ?: How do I get to your island?
textes.Comment ta vie a commencé, ici ?: How did your life here begin?
textes.Comment un Moaï dit-il bonjour ?: How does a Moai say hello?
textes.Comment ça va ? Ça va qu'il y a un rival: How am I? I'm a man with a rival on the other side of the island telling tall tales about him, that's how.
textes.Comète repasse l'anneau d'or la première: Comète flies through the golden ring first: “VZIIIOU! I win!” She does a happy loop-the-loop. “Come on, rematch! Fly through the golden ring whenever you like!”
textes.Comète t'attend près de l'anneau d'or, a: Comète is waiting near the golden ring, above the Spaceport. Fly through it to start the race!
textes.Comète, depuis sa soucoupe : « Vziiiou !: Comète, from her saucer: “Vziiiou! No walking! Hop into your Star Glider (N key) and fly through the golden ring!”
textes.Comète, la pilote de soucoupe, s'ennuie: Comète, the saucer pilot, is bored: nobody wants to race her. Now that you have the Star Glider, she challenges you: first a practice run on the ring course of the Zero-Gravity Garden, then the great ring race in the sky, around Astralys.
textes.Comète, tu cherches un adversaire ?: Comète, are you looking for an opponent?
textes.Corentin ? Le petit-fils de Yann-le-Borg: Corentin? Yann-le-Borgne's grandson? Ha! Yes, I have the logbook. Here it is… But look: the pages that talk about the seal are blank. Moon ink, the sailors called it: it can only be read by the light of a moon you carry with you. I never understood it. Keep it, it may speak to you one day. And since you're chasing after the seals: ours, the desert one, sleeps beneath the walking dune. Rachid, the carpet merchant, has an old carpet that shows the way. He'll tell you… if he stops going on about his prices.
textes.Corentin, de Carène, cherche le journal: Corentin, from Carène, is looking for the Leviathan's logbook.
textes.Couic ! Biscotte surgit de nulle part et: Squeak! Biscotte appears out of nowhere and climbs onto your shoulder.
textes.Couleurs de Gaston, en poisson. On ne le: Gaston's colours, as a fish. Found only in the jungle bay. Restores two hearts.
textes.Coups de marteau, copeaux qui volent, un: Hammer blows, flying wood shavings, a night of work… and here is the Sloop! Its cabin still smells of varnish. It's waiting for you at the pleasure-boat jetty.
textes.Courir coûte deux fois moins d'endurance: Running costs half the stamina, and you run 10% faster.
textes.Courir de la fontaine de la place à la p: Run from the fountain on the square to the lighthouse door in under 60 seconds
textes.Course abandonnée. Retourne à la fontain: Race abandoned. Go back to the fountain to try again.
textes.Coyotl demande si c'est vous qui m'envoy: Coyotl asks if you're the one who sent me.
textes.Coyotl et ses manières ! Oui. Dis-lui qu: Coyotl and his manners! Yes. Tell him that Cuauhtli the Eagle sends you, and that Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Coyotl, le potier d'Aztlán, façonne les: Coyotl, the potter of Aztlán, shapes Tlaloc's rain jars; but he only gives one away if the high priest sends you to ask.
textes.Creuser (pelle en main) là où l'ombre du: Dig (shovel in hand) where the shadow of the Houseboat's mast touches the sea at noon: on the sand, between the mast and the water
textes.Creuser le sable près de la paillote, au: Dig in the sand near the beach hut, at the water's edge (shovel in hand)
textes.Croquer un piment infernal devant le Pro: Bite into an infernal chili in front of Professor Malachar (Zébuline sells them at the Great Market)
Cuauhtli sent me: Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre d'Aztlán, cher: Cuauhtli, the high priest of Aztlán, is looking for someone to offer rain to Tlaloc and fire to Huitzilopochtli at the top of the Great Temple, and to go down beneath the temple, into the hall of the Five Suns.
textes.Cueillir cinq bouquets de cempasúchil su: Pick five bouquets of cempasúchil on the chinampas, south and west of the lake of Aztlán
textes.Cueillir cinq fleurs de braise sur les p: Pick five ember flowers on the slopes of the Great Blaze (away from the lava flows)
textes.Cueillir les cinq champignons de lune, a: Pick the five moon mushrooms at the edge of the forest ponds around Ramure (the big pond west of the Circle, the pond in the Games Clearing, and the ones to the west, south and north)
textes.Cueillir trois champignons des bois dans: Pick three wild mushrooms in the Twisted Wood (south-west of the island)
textes.Cueillir trois touffes d'herbe à fièvre: Pick three tufts of feverweed at the water's edge in the Drowned Marsh (west of the island)
textes.Cueillir un Arc-en-ciel, aux lamelles de: Pick a Rainbow, with gills of every colour (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Babillard, qui fait de petit: Pick a Chatterbox, which makes little noises when you come near (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Bolet-Ressort, au chapeau or: Pick a Spring-Bolete, with its bouncy orange cap (in the Spore Cathedral, the old gasholder south of the town)
textes.Cueillir un Petit-Géant, minuscule mais: Pick a Little-Giant, tiny but very proud (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un bouquet de tournesols dans l: Pick a bunch of sunflowers in Granny Sunflower's garden (in the Flower Camp, south-west of the campfire)
textes.Cueillir une Lunaire, pâle et argentée (: Pick a Moonling, pale and silvery (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Côté est, la mer est plus profonde. Les: On the east side, the sea is deeper. The big groupers hang around there. Bring me one, I'll pay you well.
All right, I'll take care of it.
textes.D'accord, je rentre au Temple. Que l'Aub: All right, I'll go back to the Temple. May the Dawn watch over you… and over your socks.
textes.D'accord. Je retourne à mes livres. Merc: All right. I'll go back to my books. Thank you for taking me along…
textes.DING DING DING ! Mélusine hurle depuis l: DING DING DING! Mélusine shouts from the Town Square: “ALERT! ALERT! All adventurers to the Southern Fields: THE TURNIPS HAVE WOKEN UP! Catch them before they replant themselves!”
textes.DONG… DONG… La cloche du Léviathan réson: DONG… DONG… The Léviathan's bell echoes through the whole hull. Somewhere, Ewen shouts: “It wasn't me!”
textes.Dans la Bergerie du Vent, j'ai vu une lu: In the Wind Sheepfold, I saw a moon above a pond and a sluice gate.
textes.Dans la baie de la jungle, il y a des po: In the jungle bay there are parrotfish. They're every colour under the sun and they bite like lawyers.
textes.Dans la longue-vue, toute l'île, en noir: In the spyglass, the whole island, in black and white…
textes.Dans la poche d'un vieux manteau :: In the pocket of an old coat:
textes.Dans le Glisseur stellaire ! La coque vi: In the Star Glider! The hull hums softly, the lights come on one by one.
textes.Dans le berceau : « Rrr… pfff… rrr… » Le: In the cradle: “Zzz… pfff… zzz…” The baby dwarf is already snoring like a forge.
textes.Dans le coffre : des jouets, une épée en: In the chest: toys, a wooden sword, a one-eyed teddy bear. Nobody.
textes.Dans le coffre : quarante pièces… et le: In the chest: forty coins… and the Crystal of the Dawn, warm as a rising sun. It will fit into the Seal of Winds, in front of the keep.
textes.Dans le coffre de la salle d'armes : qua: In the armoury chest: forty coins, a gold coin… and the Crystal of the Dusk, cold and blue as the evening. The Seal of Winds is waiting for it.
textes.Dans le coffret, au pied du sarcophage :: In the casket, at the foot of the sarcophagus: the last piece of Osiris.
textes.Dans le sable, deux bouteilles de limona: In the sand, two bottles of lemonade buried to keep cool, with a label: “To share.”
textes.Dans le tombeau du désert, une fresque m: In the desert tomb, a fresco shows a sheepfold beneath the mountain.
textes.Dans ton sac, le journal de bord se met: In your bag, the logbook starts to glow! In the Moonglow, silver lines appear on the blank pages: “I entrusted the Seal of Sea Spray to our Figurehead Lady. She will only give it back to whoever shows her her three sisters: the sands, the bronze and the mists. — Yves Kerhervé, last captain of the Léviathan.”
textes.Dans un cliquetis, les trois armures de: With a clatter, the three suits of armour in the armoury turn their heads toward you… and draw their swords.
textes.Dans un coin, un berceau. Dedans, un tou: In a corner, a cradle. Inside, a tiny dwarf sleeping, fists clenched like two little hammers.
textes.Dans un tombeau qui ne crache plus de fl: In a tomb that no longer spits flames: a vial of sap and a handful of coins. (The owner has gone on vacation.)
textes.Danser le pogo à un concert de la Halle: Join the mosh pit at a Howling Hall concert
textes.Danser à la Nuit des Lanternes: Dance at the Night of Lanterns
textes.De l'autre côté de l'île, à l'est, un vi: On the other side of the island, to the east, an old grump lives perched in a tree. Octave Taillefer. He sells shovels that bend and swords that rust. Don't tell him you know me.
textes.De l'herbe, de la terre, et pas le moind: Grass, earth, and not the slightest eye. This one is looking at its feet… which it doesn't have.
textes.De la brume du matin, cueillie sur la gr: Morning mist, gathered over the big pond and bottled by Pivoine. It swirls gently behind the glass.
textes.De mon temps, les voitures roulaient par: In my day, cars drove on the ground. They did, really.
textes.De plus en plus souvent, les robots démé: More and more often, Mr Lisse's mover robots land on the quays to clear out the squats. Mamie Barricade would like you to help the Boucan fight off the next Movers' Raid.
textes.De quoi veux-tu parler ?: What do you want to talk about?
textes.De quoi voulez-vous parler ?: What would you like to talk about?
textes.De retour au sommet du Grand Temple, ent: Back at the top of the Great Temple, between Tlaloc and Huitzilopochtli.
textes.De retour au sommet du Temple de Kukulka: Back at the top of the Temple of Kukulkan. The sun, at last.
textes.De retour dans la nef de la Cathédrale-F: Back in the nave of the Forge Cathedral. It's nice and warm here.
textes.De retour sur le plateau de Rê, devant l: Back on the plateau of Ra, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.De retour à la lumière, devant la Porte: Back in the light, in front of the Gate of the Four Seals.
textes.Debout, matelot ! Le soleil se lève sur: Rise and shine, sailor! The sun is rising over the sea.
textes.Dehors ! Comme la dernière fois. Mais pl: Out! Like last time. But faster.
textes.Demain, pêche à cinq heures. Qui vient ?: Tomorrow, fishing at five. Who's coming?
textes.Demander conseil à Perroquet-Joe (son ét: Ask Perroquet-Joe for advice (his stall is on the square of Port-Coutelas, near the well)
textes.Demander des pâtes fraîches à Mamma Lasa: Ask Mamma Lasagna for fresh pasta (at the Pasta Drying Shed in the daytime, at the oven on the Borgo's little piazza at noon and in the evening)
textes.Demander la Clé du Brasier à Frère Cendr: Ask Brother Cendrin for the Brasier key (in the Forge Cathedral, near the Ember Heart)
textes.Demander un grimoire à Théophraste Filan: Ask Théophraste Filandre for a spellbook, at the library (the big slate building, on the way up to the Academy)
textes.Demander une carte stellaire à Sextant (: Ask Sextant for a star chart (in the morning on the Gate lookout, around noon at the Museum, in the afternoon on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Cargo, le grand androïde dock: Ask Cargo, the big docker android on the Drone Quay (north of the city), if he has a Z-Series voice chip
textes.Demander à Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre (au: Ask Cuauhtli, the high priest (at the foot of the Great Temple), to send you to Coyotl
textes.Demander à Lucas, le docker, le nom de s: Ask Lucas the docker the name of his boat
textes.Demander à Pépé Fernand le nom de sa bar: Ask Grandpa Fernand the name of his boat (on the quay, to the east)
textes.Demander à Sextant s'il a vu Plume-de-Nu: Ask Sextant if he has seen Plume-de-Nuage (he sketches on the Gate lookout in the morning, at the Museum around noon, then on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Yannick le nom de ses bateaux: Ask Yannick the names of his boats (boat hire, on the quay)
textes.Depuis que tu passes me voir, ça va nett: Since you started visiting, I've been much better. Don't tell Gaston, he's jealous.
textes.Depuis une semaine, le Grand Spaghetti V: For a week now, the Great Flying Spaghetti has been sulking: its noodles droop, its eyes stay half-shut, and the volcano rumbles more than usual. The Reverend Father Farfalle has found the recipe that will make it friends again with its followers: the Great Reconciliation dish. It needs Mamma Lasagna's pasta, a ladleful of sauce from the Cooking Pot and parmesan grated with Captain Rigatoni's Golden Grater (which he buried somewhere thirty years ago).
textes.Depuis, les nuits de teuf, le kick trave: Since then, on party nights, the kick drum carries across the island all the way to my kapok tree. Clou dances on the roof. One night, he danced with the cash box in his arms. I was picking my coins out of the ferns until dawn. In time with the beat, too.
textes.Dernier verrou ! Le virus a débranché l': Last lock! The virus unplugged the antivirus. Click the tiles to rotate them, and rebuild the path between the battery ⚡ and the antivirus ✚.
textes.Dernière question. Mon frère jaloux m'a: Last question. My jealous brother shut me in a chest and threw me in the river; then he cut my body into pieces. My wife searched for every piece and gave me back life. Since then, I rule the kingdom of the dead. Who am I?
textes.Derrière le balancier de la grande horlo: Behind the pendulum of the grand clock, hanging from a nail: a little key!
textes.Derrière le balancier, il n'y a plus rie: There's nothing behind the pendulum anymore. Just the ticking.
textes.Derrière le mur fissuré, une petite nich: Behind the cracked wall, a little niche… with an urn.
textes.Derrière le tonneau : une araignée qui t: Behind the barrel: a spider staring at you. It hasn't seen anybody either.
textes.Derrière toutes les portes, on rit. Les: Behind every door, there's laughter. The little Moai seem very mischievous… and very curious about you.
textes.Derrière un hublot qui brille : un patch: Behind a shining porthole: a Bilge Rats patch, brand new, forgotten by a very old fan.
textes.Des blocs et des gravats jusqu'au plafon: Blocks and rubble up to the ceiling. Impossible with bare hands… With a shovel, perhaps.
textes.Des bouteilles partout, et dans chacune,: Bottles everywhere, and in each one, a tiny ship. Leaning over his workbench, an old sailor holds his breath.
textes.Des boutons ! Boutons de chemise, de man: Buttons! Shirt buttons, coat buttons, trouser buttons… One day, I'll sew myself a coat out of nothing but them.
textes.Des bâtons bien droits : de futurs manch: Nice straight sticks: future handles. You've got a good eye.
textes.Des cercles de bois tressés de fil tourn: Wooden hoops woven with thread turn gently at the ends of their strings, with beads and feathers. A craftswoman knots a net by the light of the crown.
textes.Des chats. Partout. Sur le fauteuil, sou: Cats. Everywhere. On the armchair, under the table, on top of the wardrobe…
textes.Des chaussettes chauffées par une mini-c: Socks warmed by a mini-boiler at the ankle. Ideal for the highlands.
textes.Des chauves-souris ! Elles volent à haut: Bats! They fly at head height and swoop at you: strike them when they dive.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer ! Quand la gueule s'o: Hellhounds! When the jaws open and glow red, they're about to spit fire and pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer sauvages ont pris le: Wild hellhounds have taken over the lava field, east of the Great Blaze, and growl at travellers. Captain Pyrus would like someone to drive them away.
textes.Des coucous, des pendules, des horloges: Cuckoo clocks, mantel clocks, grandfather clocks… Here, there's no shortage of time.
textes.Des crabes de roche ! Gaston en a fait d: Rock crabs! Gaston had nightmares about them for ten years. Look after yourself, {surnom}, and eat before you go down.
textes.Des crabes de roche, là-dessous ? Gros c: Rock crabs, down there? Big as barrels? Watch their claws: when they go up, back off. When they come down, strike.
textes.Des crabes sortent du puits !: Crabs crawl out of the well!
textes.Des dards jaillissent des murs ! Ces dal: Darts shoot out of the walls! Those darker flagstones are trapped.
textes.Des dattes de l'oasis, apportées par la: Dates from the oasis, brought by Mbarek's caravan: brown, glossy, sweet as honey. Restores one heart.
Drawings of waves on every wall. In the middle, a tiny little Moai stares at the wall, very serious.
textes.Des diablotins ! Ils ricanent, voltigent: Imps! They snicker, flutter about… and dive at you, pitchforks first. Step aside when they crouch, then strike.
textes.Des disques partout, dans des bacs le lo: Records everywhere, in crates along the wall. On a small cabinet, a turntable waits for someone to choose.
textes.Des djembés, une flûte, des voix qui cha: Djembes, a flute, voices singing in chorus. You want to get up and dance around a fire.
textes.Des fleurs d'œillet d'Inde, orange comme: Marigold flowers, orange like the setting sun, picked on the chinampas. Their scent, they say, guides souls. Xóchitl needs them.
textes.Des gargouilles fondent du haut des nuag: Gargoyles swoop down from the clouds!
textes.Des gargouilles se sont réveillées dans: Gargoyles have woken up in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-western cliffs. They swoop down on passing ships. Captain Charbonnel, the harbour master, would like someone to drive them away.
textes.Des gargouilles, mille sabords ! Des sta: Gargoyles, shiver me timbers! Statues that fly away, can you believe it? They nest in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-west cliffs, and they dive onto my sails. Go and drive them out. They're made of stone: hit hard.
textes.Des gobelins ! Petits, rapides, une lanc: Goblins! Small, quick, with a flint spear. When one pulls its spear back, parry (F) or roll (Ctrl). Don't worry: at the first scratch, it runs off.
textes.Des gobelins ? Qu'ils viennent ! Je les: Goblins? Let them come! I'm waiting for them! Preferably one at a time.
textes.Des graines de tournesol grillées au sel: Salted roasted sunflower seeds, in a little cloth bag. Perroquet-Joe swears no parrot can resist them.
textes.Des gâteaux sur la table, des gâteaux su: Cakes on the table, cakes on the sideboard, cakes cooling on the windowsill.
textes.Des haltères partout, un tapis, et quelq: Dumbbells everywhere, a mat, and someone puffing like a steam engine.
textes.Des lanternes de lune, petit. Dedans, il: Moon lanterns, little one. Inside is a pond mushroom that glows at night, soft and blue, like a piece of moon. Every spring, I replace them. This year, my paws no longer reach down to the water… Five of them grow, at the edge of the five ponds in the forest, around the village. Would you bring them to me? Pick them gently: they're shy.
textes.Des livres du sol au plafond. Ça sent le: Books from floor to ceiling. It smells of old paper… and mystery.
textes.Des lunettes dont les verres sont des ka: Glasses whose lenses are kaleidoscopes. The whole world becomes a rose window.
textes.Des mains d'ombre sortent des dalles noi: Shadow hands rise from the black flagstones and grab you! They surely fear light… moonlight, perhaps?
textes.Des marches mouillées : on entend l'eau,: Wet steps: you can hear the water below.
textes.Des marches tièdes : en bas, ça chauffe…: Lukewarm steps: down below it's hot… no, it's COLD. No, it's tidy. Anyway, we're going down.
textes.Des marches, des marches, encore des mar: Steps, steps, more steps… They call them the Thousand Steps. Odon counted 999: he's still looking for the last one.
textes.Des ombres… Elles glissent sans bruit da: Shades… They glide silently through the gloom of Limbo. They're not very sturdy: strike them when they reach out their arms.
textes.Des partitions partout, un pupitre, et u: Sheet music everywhere, a music stand, and an artist playing with his eyes closed. Lucky for him.
textes.Des pas métalliques résonnent dans la sa: Metallic footsteps echo through the hall… The guardians won't let you go up.
textes.Des perches des mares grillées sur une b: Pond perch grilled on a bamboo stick by Caramel, the fishmonger. Crispy. Restores two hearts.
textes.Des pièces ! Gratuites ! Tu es fou… mais: Coins! For free! You're crazy… but I'm keeping them.
textes.Des plans au mur, des outils partout. Un: Plans on the wall, tools everywhere. An inventor, bent over a workbench, didn't hear you come in.
textes.Des plumes de toutes les couleurs, parto: Feathers of every color, everywhere! On a mannequin, a magnificent headdress awaits its last feather.
textes.Des poissons de toutes les couleurs nage: Fish of every color swim… in the living-room air! Bubbles rise gently from the floor.
textes.Des racines ferment l'escalier. La salle: Roots block the staircase. The hall is waiting for something: the light of the sap, perhaps, on that big knot of wood…
Thick roots block the staircase. Perhaps they'll open if the song of the fireflies is played again…
textes.Des raptors ! Ils tournent autour de toi: Raptors! They circle around you… When one crouches, hissing, it's about to LEAP: step aside! After its jump, it's dazed for a moment: strike.
textes.Des rochers partout. L'un d'eux vient de: Rocks everywhere. One of them just giggled. Rocks don't usually giggle.
textes.Des ronces noires, épaisses comme le poi: Black brambles, thick as a wrist, covered in glistening thorns. They block the whole cave entrance. The knife slides off them as if off glass.
textes.Des ronces surgissent d'entre les branch: Brambles burst from between the branches and march toward you! Carnivorous plants open their jaws…
textes.Des rumeurs ? Je n'en vends pas. Ça ne r: Rumours? I don't sell those. There's no money in it.
textes.Des rumeurs ? Je ne parle pas aux inconn: Rumours? I don't talk to strangers about important things. Come back when we're friends.
textes.Des sables mouvants ! Tu t'enfonces… Sor: Quicksand! You are sinking… Get out quickly, and stay on the flagstones.
textes.Des scorpions des sables ! Quand la queu: Sand scorpions! When the tail rises above the head, the sting is coming: back off, roll (Ctrl) or parry (F), then strike.
textes.Des spectres ! Les coups les traversent…: Specters! Blows pass right through them… Moonlight (key 4 then X; in VR, B) makes them visible, and vulnerable.
textes.Des spectres de givre ! Leur souffle gèl: Frost specters! Their breath freezes: when they lean toward you, step aside, then strike.
textes.Des statues qui tournent à deux ? C'est: Statues that turn in pairs? It's a combination lock, nothing more. Turn, count, think. Or whack it: that never works, but it feels good.
textes.Des tasses de tous les pays ! Il ne m'en: Cups from every country! I'm only missing one: the perfect cup. I've been looking for it for forty years.
textes.Des vipères noires, au fond du puits ? E: Black vipers, at the bottom of the well? They coil up before they strike, dead straight, like an arrow. Don't stand in front: one step to the side, and you take its head off on the way back.
textes.Des voix de pierre, graves et rondes, qu: Voices of stone, deep and round, making the walls vibrate. It's beautiful. Almost.
textes.Des vraies couleurs ! Le rouge d'un cora: Real colours! The red of a coral, at the bottom of the bay, west of the beach. The golden yellow of a honey pot. And the brown of a coconut. With those, I'll paint the finest canvas of my life.
textes.Des vêtements, une chaussette orpheline…: Clothes, an orphan sock… and a smell of mothballs. Nobody.
textes.Descendre au cinquième étage du Donjon d: Go down to the fifth floor of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps

textes.Descendre dans la Pyramide de Rê, traver: Go down into the Pyramid of Ra, cross the journey of the night and defeat Apophis at the bottom of the Duat
textes.Descendre dans les Neuf Cercles (la port: Go down into the Nine Circles (the iron door at the back of the Forge Cathedral), defeat the Frost Titan at the bottom of the Cocytus and bring back the Eternal Flame
