Granny Sunflower would like to make peace… but she doesn't dare.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, pourquoi regardez-vous: Granny Sunflower, why are you looking at Rainville like that?
textes.Mamie, comment arrêter Lisse pour de bon: Mamie, how do we stop Lisse for good?
textes.Mamie, que se passe-t-il quand la sirène: Mamie, what happens when the siren wails?
textes.Mamma Lasagna a encore fait trop de pâte: Mamma Lasagna has made too much pasta again. Like every day. Luckily.
textes.Mamma Lasagna, le Révérend a besoin de v: Mamma Lasagna, the Reverend needs your pasta for the sacred Dish.
textes.Manette : croix ou stick pour viser: Controller: d-pad or stick to aim
textes.Mange-Clous, je viens vous débarrasser d: Mange-Clous, I've come to rid you of the rat.
textes.Marché conclu ! Tope là, de la patte. Qu: Deal! Shake on it, paw to hand. What shall we swap next?
textes.Marché conclu. {objet}, pour {prix} pièc: Deal. {objet}, for {prix} coins. You won't regret it.
textes.Margaux n'a personne pour livrer le pain: Margaux has no one to deliver the bread to Chez Paulo, the Square Café and the Grand Hotel.
textes.Marley ! Combien de régimes, cette semai: Marley! How many bunches this week?
textes.Marley ? Il cultive ses bananes dans mon: Marley? He grows his bananas in my corner and pays me in bunches. The best tenant in the world. He only makes noise for the banana trees.
textes.Marley fait écouter de la musique à mes: Marley plays music to my banana trees, on a little box that goes boom. I sing them sea shanties. We ended up making a deal: him on even days, me on odd days. The bunches have never been so big. Gaston leans towards the boom.
textes.Marley jure qu'il n'écoute jamais ce que: Marley swears he never listens to what I confide in my banana trees. But last week, he asked me, all casual: “And Mireille, is she any better?” By Neptune's beard! I've switched banana trees.
textes.Matthias m'envoie : que savez-vous des q: Matthias sent me: what do you know about the four seals?
textes.Matthias rêve d'ouvrir la Porte aux Quat: Matthias dreams of opening the Gate of the Four Seals. The four seals must be found, one for each people of the great island: the sea spray of Carène, the sands of Tazira, the bronze of the northern shepherds, the mists of Ramure. Each seal leads to the next.
textes.Matthias, le cartographe de Carène, rêve: Matthias, the mapmaker of Carène, dreams of drawing the heart of the island. He'd like to know what the great sealed gate at the foot of Stoneheart looks like.
textes.Maître Faelar ! Vous connaissez vraiment: Master Faelar! Do you really know my song?
textes.Maître Hugues, la fontaine fait des bull: Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles
Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles…
textes.Me rendre ma canne ? Jamais de la vie !: Give me back my rod? Not on your life! It's yours now. Go fishing, {surnom}.
Giving me back my own work? Keep it. What's sold is sold.
textes.Mener la lumière de la sève jusqu'au cœu: Guide the light of the sap to the heartwood
textes.Merci ! Et un client content, un !: Thanks! And that's one happy customer!
textes.Merci ! Lune a tissé la toile, Galet a f: Thanks! Lune wove the canvas, Galet made the ropes, and I painted the door. Here, take this for the road.
textes.Merci ! Ne le dis pas trop fort : sinon: Thank you! Don't say it too loud, or we'll have to repaint the kitchen too.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux, la porte: Thanks! Come back whenever you like, the door is always open.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux. Même pour: Thanks! Come back whenever you like. Even for nothing. Especially for nothing: I'm a bit bored.
textes.Merci ! Tiens, prends donc ça pour la ro: Thank you! Here, take this for the road. Nobody leaves my house on an empty stomach!
textes.Merci ! Tu es mon plus grand fan. Mon se: Thank you! You're my biggest fan. My only fan, but the biggest.
Thanks! You hide well, you know.
textes.Merci d'avoir ramené les esprits-luciole: Thank you for bringing the firefly spirits back. The Mother Tree has been singing ever since you came.
textes.Merci de patienter : votre déménagement: Please wait: your move is in progress.
textes.Merci encore, {surnom}. Grâce à toi, je: Thank you again, {surnom}. Thanks to you, I can go home. And you can come too: the compass knows the way.
textes.Merci, merci ! Tenez, des croissants tou: Thank you, thank you! Here, some piping hot croissants. And from now on, at my place, you'll always get a little discount.
textes.Merci, mon gars. Tiens, quelques pièces,: Thank you, lad. Here, a few coins, and a bag of seeds. Plant them wherever you like. But if one day they run away… it won't be my fault. It'll be the soil of Montjoie.
textes.Merci, petite pousse. Tiens, une fleur d: Thank you, little sprout. Here, a nebula flower from my garden: it opens when you're happy. And two moon biscuits: Gloubi makes them with flour from my flowers. Don't tell him, he thinks it's a secret.
textes.Merci. Je vais lui trouver une place dan: Thank you. I'll find a place for it among my things.
textes.Mes bâtons ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé. Pa: My sticks? I haven't asked you for anything. Not yet.
textes.Mes bâtons, tu y penses ? Il m'en faut {: My sticks, remember? I need {manque}. Without a handle, a shovel is just a flat rock.
textes.Mes coquillages ? Quels coquillages ? Ah: My shells? What shells? Ah… I haven't asked you for anything yet, I believe.
textes.Mes coquillages nacrés, tu y penses ? Il: My pearly shells, have you remembered? I need {manque}. My collection is trembling with impatience.
textes.Mes couleurs ! Tu as volé mes couleurs !: My colours! You stole my colours!
textes.Mes fruits ! Tout par terre !: My fruit! All over the ground!
textes.Mes livres… Quatre. Pendant la grande te: My books… Four of them. During the great storm, they flew out the window. One is on the library roof. Another on the tallest of the Moonstones. The third on the ledge of a window in the Leaning Tower. The last in a big twisted oak in the Twisted Wood. Nobody can climb up there. But we can call them. I'll teach you.
textes.Mes moteurs ne sont pas faits pour ça. J: My motors aren't made for this. I keep going anyway.
textes.Mes pages ! (Elle les recoud dans le gri: My pages! (She sews them back into the grimoire with a needle that sews by itself… almost.) Let's see… “How to turn a bubble into a butterfly.” “How to find your glasses.” “Nettle soup.” Oh! The soup! I've been looking for it for years!
textes.Mes pages ! Les trois ! … Ce soir, au Pe: My pages! All three! … Tonight, at the Perroquet, I'll play “The Azure Waltz” for you. And that song… it will give you breath, you'll see.
textes.Mes tuyaux ! Ne touche pas à mes tuyaux: My pipes! Don't touch my pipes!
textes.Mesdames et messieurs ! Port-Azur reconn: Ladies and gentlemen! Port-Azur today honours one of its own! Here is the key to the town. From now on, all our shopkeepers will give you a discount, and you'll always have a seat on our terraces. And in our hearts. Django, music!
textes.Messager du Soleil et de la Pluie: Messenger of the Sun and the Rain
textes.Mets-toi bien en face du bloc pour le po: Stand squarely in front of the block to push it.
textes.Mettre au tapis les trois champions du p: Knock down the three harbour champions, with fists and no blades: Gros-Louis (Requin Borgne), the Silent One (Veuve Écarlate), Belle-Humeur (Morue Enragée) — you can offer them a fair duel
textes.Miaou. Miaou ? Miaaaou. Cette maison app: Meow. Meow? Meeeow. This house obviously belongs to the cats.
textes.Midi ! Le soleil est tout en haut. L'omb: Noon! The sun is right at the top. The shadows are tiny.
textes.Mille ans que je n'avais pas parlé !: A thousand years since I last spoke!
One thousand two hundred and twelve teaspoons. This one tasted the king's soup. This one stirred a dragon's tea. Well, that's what I was told.
textes.Mince ! Il est maigre comme un balai, mo: Drat! He's thin as a rake, my poor grimoire! I opened the window to let out a little draught spell, and it left with three pages! The most important ones! Well, I think so: I can't remember what was on them. That's why they're important. They flew off over the town. Find them for me, dearie. They glow a little. They're surely magic.
textes.Minos enroule sa queue autour de lui, un: Minos coils his tail around himself, once, twice, three times… “WRONG! Go back to the start of the hall, and think.” (Ombreline, the librarian, knows all the answers.)
textes.Mio, pourquoi Zéro ne fait-il que « bip: Mio, why does Zéro only ever say "beep"?
textes.Miou ronronne dans tes bras. Ramène-le à: Miou purrs in your arms. Take him back to Nebet, in Per-Hâpy!
textes.Miou, le chat roux à l'oreille tordue de: Miou, little Nebet's ginger cat with the crooked ear, has been missing for three days. Khéty says cats love the coolness of the tombs, up on the plateau of Ra.
textes.Mistral ! Ma barque te salue. Elle a enc: Mistral! My boat says hello. Her back still aches.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul client de l'île qui pa: Mistral? The only customer on the island who pays cash without haggling. Shame he makes so much noise with what he buys from me.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul homme de l'île qui fas: Mistral? The only man on the island who makes more noise than I do. I admire him, and I sleep with cotton wool in my ears.
textes.Mistral fait trembler la baie toutes les: Mistral makes the bay shake every night. I ought to complain. But his beats sound like those of the Mother Tree, when you press your ear to the bark.
textes.Mistral… Ce soir, tu pourrais jouer un p: Mistral… Tonight, could you play a little less loudly?
textes.Mmh… pas maintenant… je suis occupé… à d: Mmh… not now… I'm busy… sleeping…
textes.Mmmh… une tarte… grande comme la maison…: Mmmh… a pie… as big as the house…
textes.Moaïs : la doyenne et la légende: Moai: the elder and the legend
textes.Moaïs : le petit qui n'a jamais vu la me: Moai: the little one who has never seen the sea
textes.Mode PC classique — F11 plein écran • F6: Classic PC mode — F11 full screen • F6 ultra sharpness (GPU) • no headset needed.
textes.Mode testeur : ce lieu n'existe pas dans: Tester mode: this place doesn't exist in this version.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île Pixelithique n'est: Tester mode: Pixelithic Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île aux Moaïs n'est pas: Tester mode: Moai Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : pas de maison à visiter i: Tester mode: no house to visit here.
textes.Moi ? Charpentier et forgeron de la Moue: Me? Carpenter and blacksmith of the Stubborn Seagull, the finest three-master in the kingdom. Until the rock.
textes.Moi ? Comme un coquillage à marée haute: Me? Like a shell at high tide: full of water and delighted about it!
textes.Moi ? J'ai trois cent douze ans. C'est j: Me? I'm three hundred and twelve years old. That's young, where I come from. My mother says I'm “still very green”.
textes.Moi ? Je ne tapote pas. (Tap-tap-tap, bo: Me? I don't tap. (Tap-tap-tap, boom-tchak.) ... Well. All right. I tap. I always have. On everything. You know, every evening, I listen to the Bilge Rats from behind the Hall's door. I know all the songs. All the drum parts. And every night, the stand-in drummer gets it wrong, and in my head, I play it right. But I don't have any sticks. Dad would never have allowed it. And besides... I'm a Lisse. They'll never want a Lisse on their stage. (He looks at your hands.) You... you have drumsticks, don't you? The ones from the Great Boucan?
textes.Moi ? À mon âge, on s'endort quand on pe: Me? At my age, you sleep when you can, little leaf.
I'm scared of demons too, you know.
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je t'a: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, shall go with you! Adventure awaits us, and so does dinner!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je te: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, challenge you! Chaaarge!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je vou: I, Sir Tancrède de Tournevent, follow you! No, I lead you! No, I walk beside you! Onward!
textes.Moi, je n'ai que des papillons. … Des pa: Me, I only have butterflies. … Stone butterflies. They don't fly very well.
textes.Moins d'une minute ! Tu as des ailes aux: Under a minute! You've got wings on your feet. Here, I'll teach you my secret: breathe well, and never look back.
textes.Moins fort ? Peuchère, les nains vont en: Less loud? Peuchère, the dwarves will complain again!
textes.Momo ? Un garçon adorable qui perce des: Momo? A lovely boy who drills holes in shells. HOLES, {surnom}. I'm fond of him, but I recount my collection after every one of his visits.
textes.Mon Pépin ! Mon petit Pépin ! Il n'est p: My Pépin! My little Pépin! He hasn't come home from the Academy, and Ortie says he wanted to see the glowing mushrooms in the Ash Wood… The wood, at night, is full of wild imps! Would you go and find him? He has a little lantern, and horns as big as hazelnuts.
textes.Mon acier ne fond pas. Il se laisse fair: My steel doesn't melt. It just goes along with it, out of politeness.
textes.Mon appareil ! Et… vous avez pris une ph: My camera! And… did you take a photo with it? Oh no. Just as well. Here, for the climb.
textes.Mon appareil photo ! Je l'ai posé au bel: My camera! I left it at the lookout, at the top of the hill, to photograph the sunset, and I came back down without it. My legs won't climb back up. Would you mind?
textes.Mon cerf-volant… Le vent l'a emporté ver: My kite… The wind carried it off towards the hill, over there, above the houses. It's stuck somewhere, I'm sure of it. Can you find it? Please?
textes.Mon chapelet ! (Elle le serre contre ell: My rosary! (She hugs it to herself, then pulls away.) It's… a little sticky. It's nothing! It's nothing at all! Oh Dawn, thank you. And thank you. You went looking for something inside a frog, for me. Nobody had ever done that.
textes.Mon engrenage ! Pas une dent de cassée !: My gear! Not a single tooth broken! Look… I put it back… I turn the crank… IT TURNS! It turns! For ever! Or at least until the end of the Fair. Here, take this, and this hat: it has a fan. I don't know why I had it, but it's yours.
textes.Mon fromager ne parle pas. … Il a dit qu: My kapok tree doesn't talk. … What did it say?
textes.Mon groin a un super-pouvoir : il trouve: My snout has a superpower: it finds food.
textes.Mon histoire ? Il n'y a pas grand-chose: My story? There's not much to tell.
textes.Mon meilleur client ! Clou, sors le tabo: My best customer! Clou, bring out the stool.
textes.Mon plus grand exploit ? (Il bombe le to: My greatest feat? (He puffs out his chest, then deflates it.) Friend… I'll confess something. They're all lost in the fog. All of them. I need a REAL feat. With a witness. And sunshine. Deep in the Goblin Wood, the goblins have a camp, and a chief, and a banner decorated with the feathers from the guards' helmets. Defeat him with me, or in front of me, or even a little in my place, and bring back the banner. I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, swear to follow you afterwards to the ends of the earth!
textes.Mon péché mignon ? %s. Rien qu'en y pens: My guilty pleasure? %s. Just thinking about it makes me smile.
textes.Mon rêve ? Je n'y ai jamais vraiment pen: My dream? I've never really thought about it.
textes.Mon trésor de braise ! (Elle serre Pépin: My ember treasure! (She hugs Pépin so tight that his little horns turn red.) You, you come back to the market whenever you like: the chili peppers are yours, for life. Well, these ones. Here.
textes.Mon vieil ami ! Assieds-toi, enfin… il n: My old friend! Have a seat, well… there's no chair. Have a seat standing up.
textes.Mon village est à l'est, derrière la Sal: My village is to the east, behind the Bell Hall! Listen to the melody at the lectern, then play it again on the bells.
textes.Mon épée d'acier. Trois semaines de forg: My steel sword. Three weeks at the forge, tempered in seawater. Hold it tight: it's my masterpiece. Don't let it rust.
textes.Mon épée te va bien. Évidemment : c'est: My sword suits you. Of course it does: I forged it.
textes.Mon épée, c'est pour les combats qui vie: My sword is for the fights to come. Strange things happen at night in the jungle, {surnom}. Train on my dummies downstairs: three hits in a row, and the last one hurts.
textes.Monsieur Fil, le marchand de programmes: Mr Fil, the program seller of the Alleys, sold you his "Turbo-Adventure 3000" for a few coins. He copied it into your travel journal… and it was a virus! A fake one, luckily: it's part of the game. Glitch, the Arcade District hacker, is helping you get rid of it.
textes.Monsieur Fil, votre programme était un v: Monsieur Fil, your program was a virus!
textes.Monsieur Lisse range ses panneaux « BIEN: Monsieur Lisse is packing away his “COMING SOON” signs. He looks at the Hall. He taps his foot. In rhythm.
textes.Monsieur Prosper, le marchand de maisons: Mr Prosper, the house seller of the Upper Town, is selling the Wisteria Cottage: a bed, a fireplace, a trophy shelf and a front covered in wisteria. Three hundred coins. He exaggerates everything. Except the wisteria.
textes.Monsieur désire un café ? Il est brûlant: Would sir like a coffee? It is scalding. I know, I tasted it with my finger.
textes.Monsieur et Madame Térieur ont deux fils: Mr. and Mrs. Side have two sons. What are their names?
textes.Monsieur le Baron, vous êtes tout décoif: Baron, your hair is all over the place!
textes.Monsieur le maire est trop aimable. Si v: The mayor is too kind. If you're looking for a bed, our rooms are waiting for you. The night passes quickly here.
textes.Monsieur le maire, une holo-photo pour u: Mr. Mayor, a holo-photo for a tourist?
textes.Mont Bolognaise — chemin de la Marmite\n:
Mount Bolognese — Cooking Pot path
Caution: unpredictable sauce eruptions.
Wear a bib.
textes.Monter au sommet de la Flèche de Cristal: Fly to the top of the Crystal Spire (with the Star Glider) and give the Heart back its shards and its light
textes.Monter au sommet de la Tour Penchée en l: Levitate up to the top of the Leaning Tower (key 8 then V; in VR, left trigger) and ring the bell (E)
textes.Monter au sommet du Mont Fusain: Climb to the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Monter au sommet du Mont Fusain (le chem: Climb to the summit of Mount Charcoal (the path starts at the north exit of the clearing) and take the pot of purple at the foot of the cairn
textes.Monter dans le Village des Arbres-Maison: Climb up into the Treehouse Village
textes.Monter en haut de la Cascade d'Encre (pa: Climb to the top of the Ink Waterfall (by the Mount Charcoal path, then along the stream) and take the pot of orange by the water, on the Lip
textes.Monter jusqu'à la Marmite, en haut du Mo: Climb up to the Cooking Pot, at the top of Mount Bolognese
textes.Monter sur Astralys par le rayon d'accue: Go up to Astralys on the welcome beam (the glowing buoy, in the north-west of the archipelago)
textes.Monter vers le centre de l'île (à l'est: Go up towards the centre of the island (east of Carène) and examine the great gate at the foot of Stoneheart
textes.Monter voir Bucatini, le gardien de la M: Go up to see Bucatini, the keeper of the Cooking Pot, at the very top of Mount Bolognese (by the spiral path, in the daytime)
textes.Monter à la Terrasse du Ciel, en haut de: Go up to the Sky Terrace, at the top of the Axiom Tower
textes.Montjoie ! Ses tavernes, ses tourtes, se: Montjoie! Its taverns, its pies, its taverns…
textes.Montjoie est si jolie d'ici. On rentre b: Montjoie looks so pretty from up here. Are we going back soon?
textes.Montjoie, la ville fortifiée sur la Butt: Montjoie, the fortified town on the Hill
textes.Montjoie, la ville sur la Butte: Montjoie, the city on the Butte
textes.Montre-la à Ilyria, elle en fera une bro: Show it to Ilyria, she'll make an embroidery from it.
textes.Montre-moi ta lame. Tiens-la en main, qu: Show me your blade. Hold it in your hand, so I can see how you hold it.
textes.Montrer la fresque du tombeau à Céleste: Show the tomb's fresco to Céleste Lunette, the astronomer of Cliquetis (at her observatory)
textes.Montrer le pot d'orange à Achille (au pi: Show the pot of orange to Achille (at the foot of the waterfall in the daytime, near the Palette in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de bleu à Basile (au bord: Show the pot of blue to Basile (by the pond in the daytime, on the Brush Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de jaune à Lili (sur la p: Show the pot of yellow to Lili (on the beach in the daytime, at the swing in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de rouge à Capucine (aux: Show the pot of red to Capucine (in the White Meadows in the daytime, on the Blotter Oak terrace at noon and in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de vert à Rosalie (à la l: Show the pot of green to Rosalie (at the edge of the wood in the daytime, on the Eraser Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de violet à Gaspard (au B: Show the pot of purple to Gaspard (at the Lookout in the daytime), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer les cinq champignons à Mère Mori: Show the five mushrooms to Mère Morille (at her caravan, in the middle of the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Montrer les trois sceaux à la Dame de Pr: Show the three seals to the Lady of the Prow, the Léviathan's figurehead (right at the front of the deck, near the telescope)
textes.Montrer les étoiles de mer à Kevin, au p: Show the starfish to Kevin, at the lifeguard post
textes.Mère Averse, Mamie Tournesol vous envoie: Mother Downpour, Granny Sunflower sends you these sunflowers.
textes.Mère Brasille, la jardinière des Jardins: Mère Brasille, the gardener of the Ash Gardens, would like five ember flowers for her flowerbeds. They only grow on the slopes of the Great Blaze.
textes.Mère Morille, la sage de la Cathédrale d: Mother Morille, the wise woman of the Spore Cathedral, wants to teach you about the five fairy mushrooms that grow in the old gasholder: the Spring-Bolete, the Moonling, the Chatterbox, the Rainbow and the Little-Giant. They must be picked and shown to her. These are storybook mushrooms: in real life, you never eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Mère Morille, quels sont ces champignons: Mère Morille, what are these glowing mushrooms?
textes.Mère Sauge m'apprendra le sort de soin s: Mère Sauge will teach me the healing spell if I bring her three mushrooms from the Twisted Wood. Then I'll have to heal the injured owl that lives near Agathe's caravan.
textes.Mère-Lune, la doyenne de Ramure, change: Mère-Lune, the eldest of Ramure, changes the moon lanterns on the bridges every spring. Her old paws can no longer reach the edge of the ponds, where the glowing mushrooms grow.
textes.Mégaphone pousse les boutons de la régie: Mégaphone is pushing the buttons on the sound desk. The red one, the blue one… and the one in the middle, all the way up.
textes.Même pas une pièce ? Bon. Je te chante l: Not even one coin? Fine. I'll sing you the chorus for free, but I sing off-key on purpose.
textes.Même si, aujourd'hui, le cœur n'y est pa: Even if my heart isn't in it today.
Right? {Il}'s just like that, {nom}. I'll pass it on, it'll make {son} day.
textes.N'installe jamais un programme qui vient: Never install a program that comes from a stranger, even if it's cheap. And never click on big shiny buttons: close windows with the little cross!

textes.NOTE DE SERVICE n° 4 512-B. « Pour desce: STAFF MEMO No. 4 512-B. “To go down, stamp the forms in the regulation order: THE SKY before THE SUN, THE SUN before COTTON CANDY. (Do not ask why. It is the procedure.) — Management.” Three offices have a coloured form: a blue one, a yellow one, a pink one.
textes.Nadine voudrait que des cartes postales: Nadine would like postcards from Port-Azur to reach the four corners of the archipelago.
textes.Nager jusqu'au nénuphar géant, au milieu: Swim to the giant water lily in the middle of the Rubbed-Out Pond and take the pot of blue
textes.Ne bouge pas, je te soigne ! Voilà, comm: Hold still, I'll heal you! There, good as new. Almost.
textes.Ne bouge pas, petit pigeon. Je ne fais q: Don't move, little pigeon. I'm only… looking.
textes.Ne bougez plus, je fais une photo avec l: Don't move, I'm taking a photo with the glow sticks!
textes.Ne frappe jamais personne. Ici, tout le: Never hit anyone. Around here, everyone has a long memory.
textes.Ne les casse pas ! Recommandation numéro: Don't break them! Recommendation number three!
textes.Ne me parle pas. Je suis de très mauvais: Don't talk to me. I'm in a very bad mood. Buy something or go away.
textes.Ne pas toucher les hélices. Elles morden: Do not touch the propellers. They bite.
textes.Ne te presse pas. Une île, ça se découvr: Don't rush. An island is something you discover slowly.
Don't touch, look with your eyes.
textes.Neuf ! Comme les vies d'un chat. C'est p: Nine! Like a cat's lives. It's handy, that makes one cat per life.
Nine. And that was the last one.
textes.Nimiel te suit partout, hein ? Elle veut: Nimiel follows you everywhere, doesn't she? She wants to know everything about humans. Everything.
Nimiel wants to know everything about humans. Everything. She's like me, three centuries ago. Only much noisier.

The rules: we hide in the city, wherever we like, but not in the planets of the fountain. That's Quark cheating. Not in the Spire either, Volt doesn't like it. You have to find both of us! Close your eyes and count to a thousand! ... Okay, to ten. Heavyfeet count too slowly.

It won't be bubbling anymore.

textes.Octave ? Le meilleur charpentier du roya: Octave? The best carpenter in the kingdom and the worst helmsman on the ocean. Twenty-two years he's been sulking at me. Or I've been sulking at him. Nobody's quite sure any more.
textes.Octave gronde comme un orage d'été : bea: Octave rumbles like a summer storm: lots of noise, and afterwards everything is greener. His kapok tree loves him. Trees are rarely wrong.
textes.Octave, le forgeron dans l'arbre… Il gro: Octave, the blacksmith in the tree… He rumbles like a storm, but he strokes the bark of his kapok tree when he thinks nobody's looking.
textes.Octave… regrette ? Vraiment ? Hmm. Il m': Octave… regrets it? Really? Hmm. He did make me the finest fishing rod in the world, after all. Don't tell him I said that.

textes.Oh ! Belle mousse ! … Et belle moustache: Oh! Lovely foam! … And a lovely chocolate mustache, too. Here, you earned it.
textes.Oh ! Tu es venu me voir chez moi ? Quell: Oh! You came to see me at home? What a nice surprise! Make yourself at home.
textes.Oh ! Tu es venu me voir dans ma yourte ?: Oh! You came to visit me in my yurt? Sit down on a pouf, I'll heat some water.
textes.Oh ! Un humain, au Royaume des Racines !: Oh! A human, in the Kingdom of Roots! I'm Lumi, a root fairy. The spirits opened the door for you… so I'll be your guide!
textes.Oh ! Un public ! Je répète pour la fête: Oh! An audience! I'm rehearsing for the neighborhood party. Want to hear my piece?
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Un vrai, avec des jam: Oh! A visitor! A real one, with legs and everything! Welcome to my humble shack, {surnom}. I'm Barnabé Coquillard, cartographer, castaway and collector.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur, à cette heure-ci ? On: Oh! A visitor, at this hour? We're playing a game of dice. Would you like some herbal tea?
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau}, pour moi ? Tu es: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}, for me? You're a treasure, {surnom}. Gaston, look!
textes.Oh ? Qu'as-tu donc pour moi ?: Oh? So what have you got for me?
textes.Oh ? Tu n'as rien que tu puisses offrir,: Oh? Looks like you've nothing to give. Never mind: your visit is enough for me.
textes.Oh non ! Je ne peux pas foudroyer la gre: Oh no! I can't zap the frog… well, I can, but gently!
textes.Oh non oh non oh non ! J'ai raté la poti: Oh no oh no oh no! I botched the beauty potion, and now… the master is a FROG! One ingredient is missing to reverse the spell. But which one?! Help me!
textes.Oh oui ! J'ai écrit quatre cartes postal: Oh yes! I've written four postcards for people everyone talks about here: Barnabé, the old man of the jungle; Lyra, the elf; Ulfa, the dwarves' innkeeper; and… the queen of the sunken city, if she exists. You travel a lot. Would you mind delivering them?
textes.Oh, de la visite ! Les chats adorent la: Oh, a visitor! Cats love visitors. Well… some of them.
textes.Oh, elles sont belles ! Tiens-les contre: Oh, they're beautiful! Hold them against you. Close your eyes. Don't think about going up: think about weighing nothing. … See? Your feet! They're not touching anything anymore! Now, the Leaning Tower: its bell hasn't rung since the great storm, the staircase collapsed. But you, you don't need a staircase anymore.
textes.Oh, mon petit, tu es tout maigre ! Mange: Oh, my dear, you're so skinny! Come on, eat something.
textes.Oh, oui ! La Nuit des Lanternes ! Il fau: Oh, yes! The Night of Lanterns! The seven Great Lanterns must be lit: the ones at the harbor, the market, the arena, the baths, the Academy, the Forge Cathedral and this one here, on the Main Square. Take my ember lantern: its flame never goes out. And ask Zigomar if his rockets are ready. After that… night falls, and we dance!
textes.Oh, oui, mon petit ! Je suis toute seule: Oh, yes, my little one! I'm all alone, Noisette has gone off following an adventurer, and I still have three loaves to deliver! One for Granny Rissole, at the Guild tavern. One for Aurore, at the castle, right at the top: without her bread, the Baron puts on his mourning hat. And one for Gilles, at the North Gate. If he's asleep, put it under his nose: he'll wake up. Here, here are the three. Don't eat them on the way! Well… not all of it.
textes.Oh, pas grand-chose. Un sourire, une bon: Oh, not much. A smile, some good news.
textes.Oh, qu'elles sont belles ! L'œil clair,: Oh, aren't they beautiful! Clear eyes, red gills… Perfect. Come back in three hours. No, I'm joking: I already had one on the fire.
textes.Oh, un Pied-Lourd ! Bienvenue ! Excuse l: Oh, a Heavyfoot! Welcome! Excuse the mess: I forgot to turn the gravity regulator back on again. Shall I turn it on?
textes.Oh, vous tombez bien ! Mon livreur s'est: Oh, perfect timing! My delivery boy sprained his ankle playing pétanque. This basket has to go to Paulo, to Gisèle at the café and to Edmond at the hotel. Would you mind?
textes.Oh. Oui. (Bzzt.) … Ça arrive. J'ai lu qu: Oh. Yes. (Bzzt.) … It happens. I read something. In a book that Madame Olga lent me. At random. Storm crystals, at the top of the Fangs, drink lightning and send it straight ahead. Not at the hat. Not at the hair. Straight ahead. I'd need three. But if I go up there alone, the storm and I will fight over the lightning bolts. Would you please… ?
textes.Oh. Pardon, monsieur le mystérieux. Gast: Oh. Pardon me, Mister Mysterious. Gaston, we've got a mysterious one.
textes.Oh. Tu as trouvé. Bon… ne dis rien à per: Oh. You found it. Well… don't tell anyone.
textes.Ohé ! Tu as une épée maintenant ? Fais a: Ahoy! You've got a sword now? Careful where you point it, I've got sails to mend.
textes.Ohé, Octave ! Ta barbe a poussé : douze: Ahoy, Octave! Your beard has grown: twelve inches, at least.
Oh… A human, here, in the heart of the trees. Don't be afraid: my name is Lyra Sylvanel, and I come from Bois-Doré, the island of the elves, on the other side of the mist.
textes.Oh… oh oh oh. C'est exactement ce qu'il: Oh… oh ho ho. That's exactly what I needed. How did you know?
textes.Oh… tu as remarqué. Là-bas, sous le peti: Oh… you noticed. Over there, under the little cloud, is an old friend of mine. Mother Downpour. We fell out fifty years ago, over something silly. I'd like to send her a bouquet of my sunflowers, to tell her I'm thinking of her. But I'm too proud to go myself. Would you be my messenger? Pick a bouquet in my garden, and take it to her.
textes.On a déjà discuté prix aujourd'hui. C'es: We've already talked prices today. It's settled.
textes.On a gagné ? On a gagné ! Merci, ô Aube: Did we win? We won! Thank you, O Dawn!
textes.On a réussi… Je peux reprendre ma lectur: We did it… May I go back to my reading?
textes.On court ? On court ! ON COURT !: Shall we run? We run! WE RUN!
textes.On dit qu'un poisson-lune doré nage au l: They say a golden sunfish swims out at sea. If you catch it, I'll buy it from you for a fortune. Barnabé will never have enough shells to pay for it, not him.
textes.On dit que l'île flottante au-dessus de: They say the floating island above your village was put there by a giant child playing dice.
textes.On dit que les cuisses de grenouille son: They say frog legs are delicious. I'm just saying it for science.
textes.On dit que sans toi, {qn} y serait encor: They say that without you, {qn} would still be stuck. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.On dit que sans vous, {qn} y serait enco: They say that without you, {qn} would still be stuck. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.On entend des ronflements. Puis un siffl: You hear snoring. Then a whistle. Then more snoring.
textes.On entend un gloussement étouffé. Quelqu: You hear a muffled giggle. Someone is playing hide-and-seek… and is counting on you to seek.
textes.On gratte, on ponce, on vernit : retour: Scrape, sand, varnish: back to the original wood. It has its charm.
textes.On joue ? On joue ? On joue ?: Wanna play? Wanna play? Wanna play?
textes.On joue à « 1, 2, 3, Moaï » ? C'est simp: Shall we play “1, 2, 3, Moai”? It's simple: when you look at us, we don't move. We're statues, it's our job. But when you're not looking… we move closer! If we touch you, we win. If you last thirty seconds, you win.
textes.On m'a dit que tu avais offert {objet} à: I'm told you gave {objet} to {qn}. Each to their own company.
textes.On m'a dit que vous aviez offert {objet}: I'm told you gave {objet} to {qn}. Each to their own company.
textes.On m'a dit que {qn} t'avait parlé de moi: I was told {qn} had told you about me. Small world.
textes.On m'a dit que {qn} vous avait parlé de: I was told {qn} had told you about me. Small world.
textes.On met les chaussettes AVANT le pantalon: You put socks on BEFORE your trousers!
textes.On n'est pas des rats d'égout, nous. On: We're not sewer rats, you know. We're HOLD rats.
textes.On ne casse pas ce qui n'est pas à soi !: You don't break what isn't yours!
textes.On ne joue pas avec la nourriture !: We don't play with our food!
textes.On ne l'appelle pas : on va le chercher: You don't call him: you go and get him!
textes.On ne se connaît pas, je crois. Tu es qu: I don't think we've met. Who are you?
textes.On peut passer les examens de l'Académie: Can we take the Academy exams?
textes.On peut. On ne devrait pas. Mais le Masq: We can. We shouldn't. But the Jade Mask of our kings is down there, ever since the Lords took it, and without it Kinich Ahau, our sun, rises without a face. The temple door opens only on the date when the gods created the world. Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it; so does the great stela in the square. Then… remember the Twins. They outwitted every trial.
textes.On raconte au Bois-Doré qu'un grand serp: In Bois-Doré they say a great serpent slept beneath your islands. I didn't believe it.
textes.On raconte qu'un poisson-lune doré rôde: They say a golden sunfish lurks out at sea, where the water is deepest. Nobody has ever landed it. Except maybe you, one day?
textes.On raconte que tu as frappé {qn}. Ici, o: They say you hit {qn}. That's not how we settle things around here.
textes.On raconte que tu as offert {objet} à {q: They say you gave {objet} to {qn}. Bad luck: that's the one thing {il} can't bear.
textes.On raconte que vous avez frappé {qn}. Ic: They say you hit {qn}. That's not how we settle things around here.
textes.On raconte que vous avez offert {objet}: They say you gave {objet} to {qn}. Bad luck: that's the one thing {il} can't bear.
textes.On s'assoit devant ou derrière ?: Shall we sit at the front or the back?
textes.On s'envole pas, on fait une pause aérie: We're not flying away, we're taking an aerial break.
You'll get used to it, you'll see.
textes.On t'a pas appris à saluer, terrien ?: Didn't anyone teach you to say hello, landlubber?
textes.On verse de haut, comme ça…: You pour from high up, like this…
textes.Ooooh ! Tu m'as trouvé ! Personne ne me: Oooh! You found me! Nobody ever finds me! Here, it's my treasure. Well, one of my treasures.
textes.Ooooh, un visiteur ! Ça faisait mille an: Ooooh, a visitor! It's been a thousand years since anyone woke the basin. I am the Echo, the voice of the stones. The five Singing Stones have forgotten their songs… I sing, you repeat: you touch the stones in the same order as me. Okay?

Yes, I love walking under the trees.
Yes, I do a bit of DIY.

textes.Ouille ! Les tombeaux crachent leurs fla: Ouch! The tombs spit out their flames, one row after another. Watch them, and cross when your row goes out.
textes.Oups ! On recommence : écoute bien…: Oops! Let's start again: listen closely…
textes.Oups ! Un filet de lumière te rattrape a: Oops! A thread of light catches you in mid-air and sets you down gently near the Gate. Halo sighs: “Heavy-Foots… always at the edge.”
textes.Ouverte ?! OUVERTE ! Deux cents ans ferm: Open?! OPEN! Two hundred years shut, and it's you… Wait, I'm writing this down. “Gate of the Four Seals: open. By…” I'll put “by the traveler.” Here: everything I'd saved for the expedition I never dared to make. And now, go down. Draw me what's down there. But come back. Mapmakers need people to come back.

textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG A ! Le Baron en a fait: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK A! The Baron's hat fell off in amazement! Again! Could somebody go and fetch it?
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG B ! Les bardes compose: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK B! The bards are already composing a song! It rhymes badly, but it's very long!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG C ! Montjoie a désorma: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK C! Montjoie now has a real hero… almost! Children, you may ask for autographs. No more than three each!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG D ! Notre aventurier a: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK D! Our adventurer has survived the frogs, the goblins and Miss Églantine's form! Master Hugues has serious matters to entrust to them!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! Un nouveau rang !: Hear ye, hear ye! A new rank!
textes.Oyez, oyez, OYEZ ! RANG S ! LÉGENDE DE L: Hear ye, hear ye, HEAR YE! RANK S! GUILD LEGEND! Master Hugues is weeping with joy into his pie! The shops will close for an hour! No, ten minutes! Oh, all right, five!

textes.POUF ! Ha ha ha ! Tu as vu la tête que t: POOF! Ha ha ha! Did you see the look on your face?! A teapot wagging its tail, and that didn't tip you off?
textes.PSCHHHHT ! Un jet de vapeur brûlante te: PSHHHHT! A jet of scalding steam pushes you back! The jets blow in rhythm: wait for a burst to end, then dash.
textes.PSCHHHT ! Une durite éclate ! La Grande: PSSSHHT! A hose bursts! The Great Digger roars, faster now… and calls two movers!
textes.Pandémonia, la cité aux mille lanternes: Pandémonia, the city of a thousand lanterns
textes.Par la PORTE ?! Comme un elfe ?! Un nain: Through the DOOR?! Like an elf?! A dwarf doesn't use the door when he can go through the rock. It's a matter of honor. And of dessert: she bakes pies.
textes.Par la lumière de l'Arbre-Mère…: By the light of the Mother Tree…
textes.Par ma barbe… il a de la repartie, pour: By my beard… he's got a quick tongue, for a tall one.
textes.Par mes cornes ! Trois épreuves sur troi: By my horns! Three trials out of three. (Malachar takes out a scorched parchment and sets his seal on it.) I declare you Bachelor of Flames of the Infernal Academy, with the jury's slightly singed congratulations.
textes.Parce qu'il a la bouche pleine ! … De pi: Because his mouth is full! … Of stone. Hee hee! (We won't repeat that to him, okay?)
textes.Parce qu'il a perdu sa voix… Sa puce voc: Because he lost his voice… His voice chip is broken. Dad says it's a very old chip, a Z Series, and they don't make them anymore. But Dad fixes everything! He just has to find the part. Will you help Dad? He's at his workshop, in the Alleys. Please, please, please!
textes.Parce qu'il a trop de problèmes !: Because it has too many problems!
textes.Parce qu'il lui manque son cœur ! L'engr: Because it's missing its heart! My grandfather's golden gear: fourteen teeth, solid gold, my name engraved on it. During yesterday's demonstration, it jumped off its axle, rolled across the square, went past the balustrade… and fell off the cliff. Down to the port, I think. Me, I'm afraid of heights, and the cable car makes me seasick. Would you mind going to have a look?
textes.Parce qu'ils sont en pierre… polaire !: Because they're made of stone… and lined with fleece!
textes.Parce qu'on voit à travers !: Because you can see right through them!
textes.Parce qu'à chaque fois, c'était incroyab: Because every time, it was incredible.
textes.Parce que c'est la CATASTROPHE ! Cette n: Because it's a CATASTROPHE! Last night, Lisse's robots got into the Hall. Politely, apologising, but they got in. They took Germaine, Clou's guitar. Clou didn't say a word. He said nothing even louder than usual. They also took the amp, and the drumsticks! And the Great Boucan is coming soon: guests will come from all the islands! Ferraille saw robots carrying a guitar toward the Grey Factory; an amp might be lying around at the Scrapyard; and Tornade swears a robot dropped something at the Dry Dock. Will you help us? You'll be our hero. Our roadie-hero.
textes.Parce que dans l'eau poivrée, ils éternu: Because in pepper water, they sneeze!
textes.Parce que la mer, ils l'ont déjà vue. Un: Because they've already seen the sea. Once. In 1342. It was wet.
textes.Parce que le rouge est parti ! Le pot nu: Because the red is gone! Pot number three. A rabbit rolled it away, I'm sure of it: I saw it dash toward Mister Straw, my scarecrow, in the middle of the Meadows. But the grass is so tall! And I'm afraid of rabbits. They have ears far too big, they hear everything you think. Would you go?
textes.Parce que sinon, ils tombent dans le bat: Because otherwise they'd fall into the boat!
Sorry! I got the wrong door.
Sorry. Excuse me. I'm going to push you.
textes.Pardonner… C'est bien un mot de client,: Forgive… Now that's a customer's word. Costs nothing to say. … I'll think about it. Don't repeat that.
textes.Parfait ! C'est exactement ce qui devait: Perfect! Exactly what was supposed to happen!
textes.Parfait ! … Enfin, presque. Tiens, pour: Perfect! … Well, almost. Here, for your trouble: my latest invention. Don't ask me what it's for.
textes.Parfait, parfait ! Vous voilà presque ci: Perfect, perfect! You're almost a citizen now. Here, a few coins, and here is a detailed map of our town: I had it added to your journal. And don't hesitate to help our residents: Port-Azur knows how to say thank you.
textes.Parfait. (Pyra pose une bûche dans sa ma: Perfect. (Pyra sets a log in her bare hand and blows on it: it bursts into flame.) Your turn. Hold out your hand. Feel the heat. Don't hold it back: push it out in front of you. … HA! A fireball! A small one, but a real one! Now, the five braziers of the Ground. All five, one after the other: each one goes out after a minute and a half.
textes.Parfait. Le Lord de la douze réclamait s: Perfect. The Lord in number twelve has been demanding his croissants since dawn. He feeds them to the seagulls, but he demands them.
Perfect! Silver all the way to the root. (He grinds them in a mortar with honey and a drop of syrup.) A spoonful each, morning and evening, and in three days they'll be fighting like ragpickers again. Which isn't necessarily good news for me.
Tell me about the people you know.
Tell me a little about yourself.
textes.Parler à Germaine, la femme de Père Gaub: Talk to Germaine, Père Gaubert's wife (at the farm, in the yard in the morning and late afternoon, in the fields late in the morning, at the market in the afternoon)
textes.Parler à Gédéon après le concert (à la H: Talk to Gédéon after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day in town)
textes.Parler à Hector, l'armurier (rue du Phar: Talk to Hector, the armourer (Lighthouse Street)
textes.Parler à Jack après le concert (près de: Talk to Jack after the concert (near the stage, or the next day)
textes.Parler à Mange-Clous, le cuisinier du Re: Talk to Mange-Clous, the cook of the Requin Borgne (on the deck of the Requin Borgne in the morning, by the fireplace of the Crâne Fendu around noon, at the nets on the quay in the afternoon)
textes.Parler à Pauline, la femme de chambre (a: Talk to Pauline, the chambermaid (at the Grand Hotel: in the corridors in the morning and afternoon, in the hotel garden at noon)
textes.Parler à Rouille après le concert (à la: Talk to Rouille after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day at the Cannery)
Tell me about the Wisteria Cottage.
textes.Partez ! Jusqu'à la porte du phare !: Go! All the way to the lighthouse door!
textes.Pas assez de pièces, {surnom}. Va pêcher: Not enough coins, {surnom}. Go fishing and bring me some fish, I'll buy it from you.
textes.Pas assez de place ici pour qu'un aigle: Not enough room here for a giant eagle to land. Go to an open area.
textes.Pas assez de place pour déplier l'Alouet: Not enough room to unfold the propeller Alouette here (it needs clear ground).
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Il y a des choses qu'on: Not today. Some things you don't tell to just anybody.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: Not today. I'm not in the mood to sell. Or to talk. Or anything.
There's no deep enough water in front of you.
textes.Pas dans la Citadelle : le vent y est tr: Not in the Citadel: the wind is too violent there. Land on the Wind Perch, south of the island.
textes.Pas de caillou ?! Dans une MONTAGNE ?! V: No pebble?! In a MOUNTAIN?! Go pick one up outside, big fella. They're everywhere. That's sort of the whole point of a mountain.
textes.Pas de canon à confettis à bord… Le chan: No confetti cannon on board… The Port-Azur shipyard installs a very pretty one.
textes.Pas de chichis ! Tiens. Tu me remerciera: No fuss! Here. You'll thank me later.
textes.Pas de longue-vue à bord… Le chantier na: No spyglass on board… The Port-Azur shipyard installs one.
textes.Pas de point de talent : gagne un niveau: No talent points: gain a level.
textes.Pas de souci ! La porte est toujours ouv: No worries! The door is always open. Like my muscles. Uh… well, you know what I mean.
textes.Pas de terre ferme sous Ventaile : survo: No solid ground beneath Ventaile: fly over an island to land.
Not from the rowboat: dock first.
textes.Pas devant mon étal !: Not in front of my stall!
textes.Pas du tout ! C'est le chat !: Not at all! It was the cat!
Not at all. I can see your feet.
Not in the middle of the sea! Dock first.
textes.Pas mal ! Trois pompes ! Bon, deux et de: Not bad! Three push-ups! Well, two and a half. It's a start!
textes.Pas mal, pas mal. Un peu de vague à l'âm: Not bad, not bad. Feeling a little at sea. But then, the sea is where I'm most at home, isn't it?
textes.Pas pendant le trajet ! Attends d'être a: Not during the trip! Wait until you've arrived.
textes.Pas pendant une éruption ! La Marmite cr: Not during an eruption! The Cooking Pot spits, step back a little…
textes.Pas trop bas, Barnabé. Les fougères s'en: Not too deeply, Barnabé. The ferns still remember.
textes.Pas une seule paire ! Rien que des chaus: Not a single pair! Only lone socks. Every one has a story. That one went around the whole archipelago inside a fisherman's boot.
textes.Pas une seule pièce ? Bon… pour toi, c'e: Not a single coin? Well… for you, it's free! A welcome gift.
textes.Pas à bord de L'Hirondelle ! Attends d'ê: Not aboard L'Hirondelle! Wait until you're on the dock.
textes.Passe-moi le parmesan, s'il te plaît. Me: Pass me the parmesan, please. Thank you. Ramen.
textes.Passer au Borgo des Coquillettes, le ham: Stop by the Borgo of the Macaroni, the followers' hamlet
textes.Passer l'épreuve du contrat avec Ombreli: Take the contract test with Ombreline, the librarian (at the Library of Souls)
textes.Passer une nuit entière à la fête de la: Spend a whole night at the beach party, in front of the great wall of sound, without hiding behind a kapok tree. Dance until the sun comes up. My people would talk about it for a thousand years.
textes.Patatras ! Tu tombes dans le bac des piè: Crash! You fall into the spare parts bin. A sorting robot picks you up, stamps you “MISCELLANEOUS” and politely sets you back at the start of the line.
textes.Pauline, Rosalie dit que Brioche aime vo: Pauline, Rosalie says Brioche likes your wool…
textes.Paulo veut des poissons pêchés du jour :: Paulo wants fish caught today: two sea bream and two mackerel.
textes.Paulo vient avec une marmite ? Ulric ave: Paulo's coming with a cooking pot? Ulric with frogs? And a fiddler pirate? (He jots it all down in his notebook, full of ink.) Stop the presses! That's the front page of the next Boucanier: “THE ISLANDS MEET AT THE BOUCAN!” And underneath, in small print: “thanks to a heroic poster courier.” That's you. Here, for your tired feet, and a zine still warm from the press.
Paused: the virus is waiting in your journal. Glitch (near the Arcade Station in the morning and evening, in the arcade hall in the afternoon) will help you resume.
textes.Pavillon rangé dans le coffre. Discret,: Flag put away in the chest. Discreet, the captain…
textes.Payer dix pièces à Églantine et poser la: Pay Églantine ten coins and lay your hand on the crystal ball (at the Adventurers' Guild counter, on the Great Square in the Middle Town)
textes.Payer trois cents pièces à Monsieur Pros: Pay three hundred coins to Mr Prosper (at his agency in the Upper Town, or in the garden of the Wisteria Cottage at noon)
textes.Peindre trois graffitis avec les bombes: Paint three graffiti with the spray paint cans (on the Expression Wall, west of the town, or on another paintable wall in Port-Boucan)
textes.Pelle, hache, épée. Rien de superflu. Et: Shovel, axe, sword. Nothing superfluous. And I buy back fish, shells and mushrooms.
textes.Pendant des années, je l'ai observé sans: For years, I watched him without his knowing. Every morning, before lighting his forge, he lays his big hand on the bark of his kapok tree and tells it: “Hang in there, old girl.” Then he grumbles very loudly, so nobody thinks he's kind.
textes.Pendant deux siècles, j'ai traversé la b: For two centuries, I crossed the mist every spring to watch over the Sacred Tree, without ever showing myself to the humans. Then one morning, I found a grey leaf at its roots. Then ten. Then a hundred. I told my mother I wouldn't come home until it could breathe again. She gave me her cloak and said nothing. Where I come from, that's like crying.
textes.Pendant la dernière tempête, l'antenne d: During the last storm, the Radio Boucan antenna blew off the mast of the Rusty Whale and landed on top of the painted water tower. Without it, Sergeant Fréquence is talking to nobody.
textes.Pendant la roulade (Ctrl), les coups pas: During the roll (Ctrl), blows pass right through you. It goes further and costs less stamina. In VR: click the left stick to dodge.
textes.Pendant une Grande Alerte des Navets (qu: During a Great Turnip Alert (when Mélusine rings her bell, in the daytime), run to the Southern Fields (south of town, through the South Gate), catch five runaway turnips with a little tap, then bring them to Père Gaubert (in his fields, near the farm)
textes.Pense très fort à un lieu que tu as déjà: Think hard about a place you have already seen… and you'll be there. Choose your destination:
textes.Personne ! Je suis un vrai fantôme ! Un: Nobody! I'm a real ghost! A ghost who has to be home before dinner, but a real one!
textes.Personne ici… pour l'instant. Allez salu: Nobody here… for now. Go and say hello to the locals!
textes.Personne n'est blessé ? Parfait, on reco: Is anyone hurt? Good, let's go again.
textes.Personne n'habite plus ici depuis longte: Nobody has lived here for a long time. It smells of dust and old wood.
textes.Personne ne le sait, {surnom}. Il y a vi: Nobody knows this, {surnom}. Twenty years ago, I was the one carrying the golden seed, the only one the Mother Tree had made in three centuries. From my boat, I saw a human on a beach dancing with a parrot. I laughed, I leaned over… and the seed fell into the water. Barnabé picked up my mistake without knowing it. I've never dared tell him.
textes.Personne ne répond. Ça sent l'encens à l: Nobody answers. It smells of lavender incense and apple pie.
textes.Personne à la maison. Une horloge fait t: Nobody home. A clock ticks. You whisper without knowing why.
textes.Personne. Juste le craquement du parquet: Nobody. Just the creak of the floorboards and the silence of a peaceful house.
textes.Personne. Mais quelqu'un a laissé un pet: Nobody. But someone left a little note: “Not here! Hee hee!”
textes.Personne. On entend juste un carillon qu: Nobody. You can only hear a chime tinkling inside, all by itself.
textes.Personne. Sur la porte, au feutre : « Pa: Nobody. On the door, in marker: “Gone to the garage. Or the café. Or elsewhere. Anyway, not here.”
textes.Personne. Une guitare débranchée est pos: Nobody. An unplugged guitar leans against the door, next to a holey umbrella.
textes.Personne. Une théière. Une théière qui t: Nobody. A teapot. A teapot that's looking at you. Teapots don't usually look.
textes.Petit poisson argenté des côtes. Rend un: A small silvery fish from the coast. Restores half a heart.
textes.Petit-Pierre, Biscotte est sur mon épaul: Petit-Pierre, Biscotte is on my shoulder!
textes.Petit-Pierre, pourquoi tu caches du pain: Petit-Pierre, why are you hiding bread in your pocket?
textes.Petites baies sucrées des buissons. Rend: Small sweet berries from the bushes. Restores half a heart.
textes.Pfff. Tu as de la chance, je suis de bon: Pfff. You're lucky, I'm in a generous mood. Fifteen percent, today only.
textes.Pfffft ! Un petit nuage sort de vos chev: Pfffft! A little cloud comes out of your ankles. Your toes thank you.
textes.Photon, vos plantes clignotent bizarreme: Photon, your plants are blinking strangely
Photon, your plants are blinking strangely…
textes.Pierre et feu ! Ton acier fond très bien: Stone and fire! Your steel melts very nicely, tall one. That's a compliment.
textes.Pigment, la graffeuse, trouve que tu as: Pigment, the graffiti artist, thinks you "look like someone who makes beautiful walls". She gives you three spray paint cans: three graffiti must be painted on the paintable walls of Port-Boucan.
textes.Pinceau sec : trempe-le dans la Palette: Dry brush: dip it in the Palette
textes.Pixel et son petit frère Quark jouent à: Pixel and her little brother Quark are playing hide-and-seek, and Quark always cheats. Pixel invites the hero to play: the two children will hide somewhere in Astralys, and both of them must be found.
textes.Pixel, tu veux jouer à quelque chose ?: Pixel, do you want to play something?
textes.Place ! Place au chevalier de Tournevent: Make way! Make way for the knight of Tournevent!
textes.Plante verte (en plastique).\nNe pas arr:
Houseplant (plastic).
Do not water. Do not love.
textes.Pleine, décroissante, nouvelle, croissan: Full, waning, new, waxing: the four dials line up, a chime of crystal… and the slate door slides away upward.
textes.Plic… plic… plonc ! Les trois gouttes to: Drip… drip… plunk! The three drops fall into the three buckets, and it almost makes a melody. “Brilliant! Thank you! I'll call it: Concerto for a Leaky Roof.” He gives you a few coins.
textes.Plic… ploc… Il pleut dans la yourte. Tro: Drip… drop… It's raining inside the yurt. Three drops fall from the roof onto the rug, and someone watches them with resignation.
textes.Plonger au pied de la pointe du phare, c: Dive at the foot of the lighthouse point, on the open-sea side, and find the lens shard
textes.Plouf ! L'Achéron est glacé… Charon te r: Splash! The Acheron is freezing… Charon fishes you out with his oar, sighing: “One obol, I said. Not a swim.”
textes.Plouf ! L'eau du lac est froide comme un: Splash! The lake water is as cold as a winter morning. You climb back onto the shore, shivering; the frogs are laughing (well, croaking). Hop from stone to stone!
textes.Plouf ! L'eau noire du bassin amortit ta: Splash! The black water of the pool cushions your fall.
textes.Plouf ! Tu nages dans l'eau froide jusqu: Splash! You swim through the cold water to the entrance ledge and haul yourself up, soaked.
textes.Plouf ! Tu remontes, trempé, sur le rebo: Splash! You climb back out, soaked, onto the entrance ledge. The basin is too deep to swim in.
textes.Plouf ! Tu te poses dans l'eau. L'Alouet: Splash! You land in the water. The Alouette, soaked, folds back into your bag. Time to swim!
textes.Plume-de-Nuage file sous la grande verri: Plume-de-Nuage darts under the great glass roof of the Greenhouse, does three happy loops among the other creatures of the sky, and comes back to brush your cheek. She's home! Go and tell Nova.
textes.Plume-de-Nuage s'est arrêtée : tu vas tr: Plume-de-Nuage has stopped: you're going too fast, she's afraid of getting lost. Go back for her!
textes.Plume-de-Nuage, la plus jeune méduse de: Cloudfeather, Nova's youngest sky jellyfish, has escaped from the Greenhouse of Species. She's floating somewhere around the island and can't find her way home on her own. Sextant, who draws the island from the lookouts, may have seen her go by.
textes.Plus calme… (Il regarde le lac longtemps: Calmer… (He looks at the lake for a long time.) It's true. You can hear the ducks. I hadn't heard the ducks in years. Here, my friend: frog legs for Ulric, he'll cook them for you. And my eternal gratitude. It's very big, my gratitude. Like my fears.
textes.Plus de toit, plus de porte, plus de sou: No more roof, no more door, no more eyebrows! My fifteenth roof, I want to make it out of iron. Thick iron. I need three blocks of iron ore. The shepherds of the north sell it, so do the dwarves of Fire Mountain, and you can find some by digging in the rocks. Bring me three, and I'll give you… something. Something pretty. That doesn't explode.
textes.Plus faim ? À ton âge ? Allons donc ! Ti: Not hungry? At your age? Nonsense! Here.
textes.Plus jamais de potion le lundi !: No more potions on Mondays, ever!
textes.Plus rien ! Tu as tout mangé, petit gour: All gone! You ate everything, little gourmand. Come back tomorrow, I'll make more!
textes.Plus un seul pot à chercher : ils sont t: Not a single pot left to find: they've all been found!
textes.Pointus… Bon. Chacun ses défauts. Je ne: Pointy… Well. Everyone has their flaws. I'm not judging you. Well, a little.
textes.Port-Azur — la perle de l'archipel: Port-Azur — the pearl of the archipelago
textes.Port-Boucan, la ville libre du vieux por: Port-Boucan, the free town of the old harbour
textes.Porte de cuivre.\nLa clé ? Demandez\naux:
Copper door.
The key? Ask
the frogs.
textes.Porter le bouquet à Mère Averse, à Rainv: Take the bouquet to Mother Downpour, in Rainville (in the daytime, in the street or on the terrace of the Feedback Café)
textes.Porter le rouage à Hortense, devant la m: Take the cogwheel to Hortense, in front of the town hall
textes.Porter un pain à Aurore (au château, au: Take a loaf of bread to Aurore (at the castle, at the top of the Hill: take the winding ramps all the way up)
textes.Porter un pain à Gilles (le garde de la: Take a loaf of bread to Gilles (the North Gate guard, in the Lower Town, near the harbour)
textes.Porter un pain à Mamie Rissole (à la tav: Take a loaf of bread to Mamie Rissole (at the tavern, at the back of the Adventurers' Guild)
textes.Porter une affiche à Paulo (à Port-Azur,: Take a poster to Paulo (in Port-Azur, at his restaurant Chez Paulo, on the harbour, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m.)
textes.Porter une affiche à Tom le Violoneux (s: Take a poster to Tom the Fiddler (on Balafre Island, in Port-Coutelas: he plays in the evening on the stage of the Crâne Fendu, and in the afternoon you can find him on the square)
textes.Porter une affiche à Ulric (sur l'Île de: Take a poster to Ulric (on Montjoie Island, at his inn "La Grenouille Repue", in the Middle Town, near the Great Square)
textes.Porter une carte postale à Barnabé (île: Take a postcard to Barnabé (Jungle Island)
textes.Porter une carte postale à Lyra, l'elfe: Take a postcard to Lyra the elf
textes.Porter une carte postale à Ulfa, à la ta: Take a postcard to Ulfa, at the Forgefer tavern
textes.Porter une carte postale à la reine de l: Take a postcard to the queen of Atlantis
textes.Porter une lettre à Gorgoth le Cornu (à: Take a letter to Gorgoth the Horned (at the arena, or at the baths)
textes.Porter une lettre à Grumbald (au comptoi: Take a letter to Grumbald (at the counter of the inn "Au Diable Repu", at the port)
textes.Porter une lettre à Ombreline (à la Bibl: Take a letter to Ombreline (at the Library of Souls, in the Upper Town)
textes.Poser le Plat de la Grande Réconciliatio: Place the Great Reconciliation dish on the altar of the Colander Temple
textes.Poser le fromage près de la cale du Requ: Put the cheese down near the hold of the Requin Borgne and wait for Biscotte to come out of his hole: if he climbs onto your shoulder, you've won
textes.Poser les quatre sceaux dans la Porte au: Place the four seals in the Gate of the Four Seals, at the foot of Stoneheart
textes.Poser les trois reliques sur l'Autel des: Place the three relics on the Altar of the Three Suns
textes.Posez la main, bien à plat… (La boule s': Place your hand, nice and flat… (The ball lights up, hesitates, goes “bzzz”, then displays golden letters.) Let's see: Strength, decent. Agility, enthusiastic. Magic, “maybe later”. Luck, “hmm”. Appetite: EXCEPTIONAL. Hidden talent: “knows how to get back up”. (She stamps three times.) Congratulations! Here is your Adventurer's Card. Rank F. Like everyone else. Even Master Hugues, at the start. Especially Master Hugues.
textes.Posé ! E pour replier l'Alouette, Espace: Landed! E to fold the Alouette, Space to take off again by pedalling.
textes.Posé en douceur ! L'Alouette se replie d: Soft landing! The Alouette folds back into your bag.
textes.Pots de peinture ouverts, pinceaux prêts: Paint pots open, brushes ready! I've put you in navy blue for now; choose your colour.
textes.Pouah ! Recraché comme un noyau de ceris: Ugh! Spat out like a cherry pit! You're dripping with green slime.
textes.Pouf… je souffle une minute. Une petite: Phew… I'm catching my breath for a minute. Just a little minute.
textes.Pour Nâga, souviens-toi : la tête à terr: For Nâga, remember: when its head is on the ground, you strike. And when it dives, the three Eyes… like on the fresco in the lair, I bet.
textes.Pour Zéro ? … Oui. J'en ai gardé une. Un: For Zéro? … Yes. I kept one. Just one. I knew someone would need it one day. I didn't know it would be him. It's in a little black box, resting against the orange container: west of the jetty, the first container, the one that's all alone. Take it. Gently.
textes.Pour accepter des contrats, recruter des: To take on contracts, recruit companions and rise in rank, you must be signed up with the Adventurers' Guild of Montjoie. Églantine, the receptionist, asks for ten coins and a little crystal-ball reading.
textes.Pour de bon ? (Elle pose son tricot.) Éc: For good? (She sets down her knitting.) Listen to me, kiddo. Lisse has a factory, to the south-east, behind the Spore Woods: the Grey Factory. Under the factory, there are five floors. Offices, an assembly line, a boiler room, a warehouse... and right at the bottom, the President's Pit, where his Great Digger sleeps, an enormous machine run by a computer. That's where he keeps the plans for the Lisse-Center. No plans, no Lisse-Center. And without the Digger, no more robots. I'm too old to go down. But you... Go down, defeat that machine, and bring me back the plans. And if you meet little Aldric down there... don't hurt him. He's a kid who forgot how to play.
textes.Pour en savoir plus sur ce problème : il:
To find out more about this problem: you shouldn't have bought it.

If you call a repairer, give them this information:
Stop code: NOT_CHEAP_AT_ALL_PROGRAM
What failed: turbo_adventure_3000.prg
textes.Pour entendre la mer… même quand ils lui: To hear the sea… even when they have their backs to it!
textes.Pour la peine, ils t'offrent un morceau: For your trouble, they give you a piece of what's on the table.
textes.Pour le Plat sacré ? (Il goûte la sauce,: For the sacred Dish? (He tastes the sauce, for a long time, eyes closed.) … It is worthy. It needs a bit of salt, but it is worthy. Take a ladleful with the Sacred Ladle, there, at the edge. Just one. And blow on it. Then go and see the Captain, on the beach: he's the one who has the Golden Grater. Well, who had it.
textes.Pour le coup de pioche, une part de tart: For the pickaxe swing, a slice of pie… and what the tunnel turned up.
textes.Pour moi ? Oh… {dernier_cadeau}. C'est d: For me? Oh… {dernier_cadeau}. How thoughtful. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Pour mon départ, Sylwen m'a fait un pain: When I left, Sylwen made me a travel loaf with honey from the Mother Tree, “that keeps for a month”. It lasted two days: a green parrot came every morning to steal a piece, squawking “Hellooo”. I found out later his name was Gaston.
textes.Pour monter son mur de son, Mistral m'a: To set up his sound wall, Mistral borrowed my rowing boat. Seventeen crossings, one speaker each time, and me at the helm with my map. Not one rock, not one scratch. I point it out to anyone who'll listen. Especially on the other side of the island.
textes.Pour sa première cabane, Gaspard a comme: For his first shack, Gaspard started with the roof. A very fine roof, sitting in the grass, with nothing underneath. I explained that you start with the floor. He nodded for an hour. Since then, he starts with the floor. And he's still nodding.
textes.Pour son mur de son, il m'a commandé qua: For his wall of sound, he ordered forty iron brackets from me. He paid cash, no arguing, tapping his foot. I was suspicious all week. Nothing. An honest customer. Apparently they exist.
For you, the best from the barrel.
textes.Pour toi, {surnom}, les prix d'ami. Enfi: For you, {surnom}, friend prices. Well, almost-friend prices.
textes.Pour vous, jeune personne, une petite bo: For you, young person, a little purse. And a standing invitation to the castle. Come whenever you like. Aurore will show you around the hat cupboards. There are forty-two of them. Set aside the whole day.
For you, the best from the barrel.
textes.Pourquoi le Grand Moaï ne dit jamais rie: Why does the Great Moai never say anything?
textes.Pourquoi le Grand Moaï ne joue-t-il jama: Why does the Great Moai never play hide-and-seek?
textes.Pourquoi le livre de calcul est-il trist: Why is the math book sad?
textes.Pourquoi les Moaïs ont-ils de si grandes: Why do Moai have such big ears?
textes.Pourquoi les Moaïs regardent-ils toujour: Why do Moai always look toward the inside of the island?
textes.Pourquoi les elfes ne jouent-ils jamais: Why do elves never play hide-and-seek with trees? … Because trees cheat: they never move.
textes.Pourquoi les fantômes sont-ils de si mau: Why are ghosts such bad liars?
textes.Pourquoi les plongeurs plongent-ils touj: Why do divers always dive backward?
textes.Pourquoi les poissons détestent l'ordina: Why do fish hate computers? Because they're scared of the net! Ha! Gaston never laughs at that one.
textes.Pourquoi les poissons vivent-ils dans l': Why do fish live in salt water?
textes.Pourquoi un arbre ? Pour voir venir les: Why a tree? To see the ships coming. And so I don't have to see Barnabé's shack.
Move over, you're blocking my light.
First lock: its surprise windows. Close them with the little cross ✕, at the top right of each window. You need eight!
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Aristide, le maire: Take a holo-photo of Aristide, the mayor of Port-Azur (at the town hall, on the square; at noon at Paulo's, in the late afternoon at the boules pitch)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Mama Grog (Île de: Take a holo-photo of Mama Grog (Balafre Island, in Port-Coutelas: at the counter of the Crâne Fendu, from 10 a.m. until late at night)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Mamie Barricade (Î: Take a holo-photo of Mamie Barricade (Boucan Island, in Port-Boucan: at the Cannery, in the assembly room on the roof, or in front of the entrance in the afternoon)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo le Baron Barthélem: Take a holo-photo of Baron Barthélemy (Montjoie Island, at the castle, at the top of the Hill: throne room in the morning, garden or rampart in the afternoon)
textes.Prendre la grande toile de Lune, roulée: Take Lune's big canvas, rolled up next to her loom (in the Flower Camp, near the northern yurts)
textes.Prendre la puce vocale Série Z, contre l: Take the Z-Series voice chip, against the orange container (the first one west of the pier)
textes.Prendre la puce vocale dans la petite bo: Take the voice chip from the little black box, against the orange container (the first one west of the pier)
textes.Prendre le parapluie aux tournesols, sur: Take the sunflower umbrella from the porch of Mother Downpour's yurt (Rainville, at the top of the main street, on the left)
textes.Prendre le rouleau de cordes que Galet a: Take the roll of ropes Galet has prepared for the stage (at the Ropeworks, in the north-west, next to the spinning wheel)
textes.Prendre une chambre pour la nuit: Take a room for the night
textes.Prends ce thé de lune, il vient de mon j: Take this moon tea, it's from my garden.
textes.Prends le temps de te reposer. Un voyage: Take time to rest. A tired traveller misses the most beautiful things.
textes.Prends ton bateau et suis la boussole :: Take your boat and follow the compass: its crystal needle always points to the Mother Tree, to the east, between your village and the jungle. The mist will part before you. I'll wait for you on the village square, at the foot of the great trees.
textes.Prends ton temps. Les gens d'ici, il fau: Take your time. Folks round here need a bit of taming.
textes.Prenez un ticket.\nPuis attendez.\nPuis:
Take a ticket.
Then wait.
Then wait some more.
textes.Prenez votre temps. Les gens d'ici, il f: Take your time. Folks round here need a bit of taming.
textes.Presque ! Les pierres ont pouffé de rire: Almost! The stones burst out laughing.
textes.Presque vide ? Elle est VIDE ! Enfin, il: Almost empty? It's EMPTY! Well, there's the label. The label is very beautiful. “The Showcase of the Islands: one object from each island below.” But I have nothing to put under it! Solenne says she never goes down. The birds only bring back twigs. And me... I don't dare go down. You travel! Bring me a seashell from the sea, near Port-Azur; a parrot feather from Balafre, the pirate island; a scarab from the Three Suns desert; a patch from the Bilge Rats, those very loud punks of the Boucan; and a golden turnip from Montjoie. They say they run. An object that runs! Fascinating!
textes.Prochain morceau : « Lever de Lune ». Pr: Next track: “Moonrise”. Get your arms ready!
I promise. You'll scare the next one.
textes.Près du feu, une vieille Moaï couverte d: By the fire, an old Moai woman covered in lichen. Around her, three tiny Moai wait for a story.
textes.Prêtes ? PRÊTES ? (Ses lunettes fument.): Ready? READY? (His glasses are smoking.) I'm missing the main thing: sulfur! Three fine crystals, from the hot springs, at the foot of the volcano, to the west. Without them, my rockets will go “pfff.” With them: KABOOM, in seven colors!
textes.Pschhht ! Évidemment ! Tout le monde peu: Pschhht! Of course! Everyone can paint here! Here: three cans of spray paint, homemade, from beetroot, spinach and blueberry. They smell a bit like soup, that's normal. Go to the Expression Wall, west of town, or any other paintable wall, and leave your mark. Three graffiti pieces! A wall is like a page of a zine, but bigger and more vertical. And don't be afraid of messing up: the wall doesn't judge. Me, a little, but kindly.
textes.Pschhh… ALERTE ! ALERTE ! Ici Radio Bouc: Pshhh… ALERT! ALERT! This is Radio Boucan: Lisse's robots are landing! Everybody outside, form a chain!
textes.Psst ! Approche, j'ai appris quelque cho: Psst! Come closer, I've learned something about you.
textes.Psst ! Approchez, j'ai appris quelque ch: Psst! Come closer, I've learned something about you.
textes.Psst ! C'est Glitch, des Arcades. J'ai v: Psst! It's Glitch, from the Arcades. I saw Mister Fil's “program” jump into your journal. I got into the system to help you. This virus is protected by three locks: we'll break them one by one!
textes.Psst… Par ici, humain. Approche, n'aie p: Psst… Over here, human. Come closer, don't be afraid.
textes.Ptoui ! La grenouille te recrache… Tu es: Ptooey! The frog spits you out… You're covered in slime. It smells of mud.
textes.Puis-je aider le jury de la Foire ?: Can I help the Fair's judges?
textes.Pyra Flammèche m'apprendra la boule de f: Pyra Flammèche will teach me the fireball if I bring her three logs of twisted wood. Then I'll have to light the five braziers of the Duelling Ground in a row.
textes.Père Gaubert, Truffe veut venir avec moi: Père Gaubert, Truffe wants to come with me.
textes.Père Gaubert, qu'est-ce qui a creusé ce: Père Gaubert, what dug this hole in your field?
textes.Pépin, le lapin qui organise la Grande C: Pépin, the rabbit who organises Ramure's Great Race, is looking for someone who can beat Bondi, the champion three years running.
textes.Pépin, le petit diablotin de Zébuline, n: Pépin, Zébuline's little imp, hasn't come home from the Academy. His classmates saw him heading off to the Ash Wood to see the glowing mushrooms.
textes.Pêcher ? Pour toi, {surnom}, oui. Tiens,:
Fishing? For you, {surnom}, yes. Here, take my old rod. Look after it, it's the only thing that came with me from the shipwreck. Along with Gaston. And my socks.

Equip it, go up to the water, hold {bouton} to wind up and release to cast. When the float dips: {bouton} again, quick!
textes.Pêcher ? Si je sais pêcher ! J'ai une vi: Fishing? Do I know how to fish! I've got an old rod, right there, under my imaginary hammock. But I don't lend it to just anyone, {surnom}. We hardly know each other.
textes.Pêcher et apporter à Paulo deux dorades: Catch two sea bream and two mackerel and bring them to Paulo
textes.Q / D : virer, Z : piquer (plus vite), S: Q / D: turn, Z: dive (faster), S: pull up (slower), E: land.
textes.QUAI DE CHARGEMENT\n(2 m : trop haut ? u:
LOADING DOCK
(2 m: too high? a crate!)
textes.QUEL CONCERT ! Tu as vu la fosse ? Tu as: WHAT A CONCERT! Did you see the pit? Did you see Granny Barricade raise her fist up on the mezzanine? Did you see Clou SMILE? I did, I saw everything, and now I've lost my voice. (She whispers.) Thank you. Without you, it would have been a tiny little racket. Here: the door takings. There was no door, it's free, so it's the takings from the donation box. And you are now, officially, forever... Number 1 Fan of the Bilge Rats.
textes.QUOI ?! QUI ?! QUELLE ANNÉE ?! … Huit ce: WHAT?! WHO?! WHAT YEAR?! … Eight hundred years?! I said “just five minutes”! … Well. Thanks, you know. Here, I dreamed about this the whole nap, I'll give it to you.
textes.Qu'elles sentent bon ! Les âmes trouvero: How good they smell! The souls will find their way this year. (She tucks one behind your ear.) That one's for you.
textes.Qu'elles sont belles ! (Elle les plante: How beautiful they are! (She plants them one by one, and the ash around them begins to glow.) They'll shine all night. Just like you, little spark.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'il y a à voir par ici ?: What is there to see around here?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un Moaï dit à un autre Moaï: What does one Moai say to another Moai?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un Moaï met sur ses frites: What does a Moai put on his fries?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un canif ?: What do you call a very small knife?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un crabe qui fait du vélo ?: What's a crab on a bicycle? A crab that goes sideways, only faster.
textes.Qu'est-ce que ce chat vous a volé ?: What did that cat steal from you?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu aimerais faire, un jour: What would you like to do one day?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu fiches chez moi ?!: What are you doing in my house?!
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu retiens de moi ?: What do you remember about me?
textes.Qu'est-ce qui a des dents mais ne mord j: What has teeth but never bites?
textes.Qu'est-ce qui est vert, qui monte et qui: What's green and goes up and down?
textes.Qu'est-il écrit au-dessus de la porte de: What is written above the gate of the Nine Circles?
textes.Quand elle s'entoure d'un bouclier d'épi: When she wraps herself in a shield of thorns, wake the three roses of light. Their light burns her!
textes.Quand il raconte l'histoire de la graine: When he tells the story of the lost golden seed, Faelar always says: “The sea took it.” Then he looks at me, one second too long. I think he knows. He's never asked me anything. That's his way of being kind.
textes.Quand j'aurai appris les six sorts des m: When I've learnt the six spells of the masters of Arcanelle, the archmage will lead me to the Moonstone Circle for the ceremony.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, Faelar nous racont: When I was little, Faelar used to tell us about the seeds of the Mother Tree, sown on every island. One evening, he fell asleep just before the end: the one about the humans' tree. He slept a whole spring. I couldn't wait. At a hundred, I asked the council to become its guardian. Nobody else wanted to cross the mist.
textes.Quand je serai grande, j'aurai des circu: When I grow up, I'll have pink circuits, like her.
textes.Quand je suis montée à son échelle, il a: When I climbed his ladder, he hid his axe behind his back, like a child hiding a cake. He offered me some herbal tea, then told me the price, then said it was a joke. I'm still not sure it was.
textes.Quand je suis tombée de la passerelle, à: When I fell from the walkway, at forty, Aëlwen bandaged my ankle with sage leaves and made me drink her potion. I pulled faces for a week. In Bois-Doré, they still call it “Lyra's grimace”. Aëlwen takes it as a compliment.
textes.Quand la sirène sonne et que Sergent Fré: When the siren wails and Sergeant Fréquence sounds the alarm on the radio (in the daytime, in town), fight off the Movers' Raid: stop the robots before they carry the furniture off to the harbour
textes.Quand la sirène sonne, mon grand, c'est: When the siren sounds, kiddo, it means Lisse's robots are landing. The movers. They go into a squat, take the sofas, the tables, the crates, and carry everything off to the harbour saying “Thank you for your understanding.” We don't understand. So we all go out, link arms in front of the door, and form a chain. A human chain. The robots hate that: it's not in their programming. Next time Sergeant sounds the alert, come help us. Stop the robots, without hurting anyone except a few bolts. And we'll hold the door.
textes.Quand tu ne sais plus quoi faire, demand: When you don't know what to do, ask people for rumours. There's always a lead.
When they bite, reel in with little turns. If the tension goes red, ease off a bit. The fish tires before you do. Normally.
Forty minutes of rain on a tent. Nothing else. “It's my favorite record to fall asleep to,” says the owner.
textes.Quatre chemins partent du carrefour : un: Four paths leave the crossroads: a red one, a black one, a white one, a yellow one. On the stele, these words: “Here, the Twins hesitated. But Xan, the mosquito, went on ahead of them.”
